# UI Build — Knowledge & Context

How UI actually gets built and verified in this codebase: Salesforce PWA Kit v10 slim
`overrides/`, Chakra UI v2.7.0, Storybook 10, Zimmermann design tokens.

Technical reference only — no roles, no process, no review workflow. Every claim below was
re-verified against the live toolchain and working tree on **22 August 2026**, not taken on trust
from where it was first learned. Where a widely-repeated belief turned out to be wrong, the
correction is marked **⚠︎ CORRECTED** with what's actually true.

---

## 1. How a value resolves

The one-way chain. Each layer may read the one above it and never the reverse:

```
theme/foundation/*.ts      source values, designer-owned — you don't add tokens here
   ↓
theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts   DERIVED output, emits --zimm-* onto :root — never hand-edit
   ↓
theme/components/<name>.ts       recipes, consuming var(--zimm-*)
   ↓
component JSX                    textStyle + semantic tokens only
```

### The registration reality

`theme/index.ts` registers **`borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space`,
`textStyles`** — and nothing else. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are
absent. Measured by bundling the live theme and evaluating `css(…)(toCSSVar(theme))`:

```
padding:  'xs 0'     →  {"padding": "xs 0"}                  // verbatim → browser DROPS it
width:    'xl'       →  {"width": "var(--chakra-sizes-xl)"}   // 36rem, not space.xl's 1.5rem
fontSize: 'l'        →  {"fontSize": "l"}                     // no such key → DROPPED
textStyle:'footer'   →  6 resolved literals, zero var()
```

| Prop family | Resolves through | Bare scale key |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` `top/right/bottom/left` | `theme.space` ✅ | **Correct** |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min\|maxWidth\|Height` | `theme.sizes` ❌ | **8×–112× wrong, or dropped** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | `theme.fontSizes` etc. ❌ | Wrong value, or dropped |

Worst measured case: `3xs` intended as 2px emits **224px**. `s`/`m`/`l` have no Chakra `sizes`
key at all, so those declarations vanish silently rather than blowing up.

**This is the single most dangerous thing in the styling layer, because the syntax is
identical.** `padding: 'xl'` is correct and `width: 'xl'` is a catastrophe. On sizing and
typography props, always the CSS var: `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`.

Live instance still in the tree: `components/header/index.tsx:302` ships `fontSize="l"`, which
emits nothing.

### `textStyle` can never emit a var — and what that means

`zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be a circular import.
`textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build time. **This is correct
behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an emitted-CSS audit flags as
"raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.**

**So the real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax.** The question to ask of any
value is *"is this typed more than once?"* — not *"is this a `var()`?"* An audit built on syntax
generates mostly noise.

### Value equality is not token equality

⚠︎ **CORRECTED.** Three constants were once flagged as "mirrors" duplicating existing tokens.
**All three were false positives.** Rewriting `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` to
`var(--zimm-scale-1200)` would have been a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression** — that token is authored in
**px**, which doesn't scale under zoom — plus a numeric-alias violation, and there is no valid
named token in the gap (the scale jumps 2.5rem → 4rem).

Before "fixing" any apparent duplicate, gate it on three checks:

1. **Same unit?** rem and px are not interchangeable; rem is required wherever text or spacing
   must scale under zoom.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A coincidental numeric match is not a relationship.
3. **Is the target a permitted token?** `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases are class-only; naming
   one from a recipe is itself a violation.

Known numeric-alias violations in the tree: `listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` and `header.ts:59`. Match
them with `var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)` — a bare `[0-9]` also matches `3xs` and inflates the count.

### Units

`rem` for anything that must scale with root font size or zoom (type, spacing). `px` only for
hairline geometry that must *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets. `em` only for
breakpoints.

---

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

**`extendTheme` deep-merges — namespace every recipe.** SFCC ships its own `Footer` recipe.
Naming ours `Footer` merged into it: copyright rendered 14px instead of 10px and the subscribe
heading lost its 24px gap. The mechanism is ordering — an existing key is overwritten *in place*,
a **new** key is appended **last**, so your `margin: 0` shorthand lands after the base's
`marginBottom` and wipes it. Hence `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmNavItem`.

**A recipe unit test cannot catch this.** In isolation Chakra emitted the correct order; the
collision only appears merged. Intentional merges are allowlisted in `recipeGuards.test.ts`:
`Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu`.

**Compound values are never tokenised.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` ships verbatim and the browser discards the declaration. Use axis props.

**Shorthand after longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` declared after `paddingBlock` silently kills
it. Use `paddingInline`.

**`IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a style prop**, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:` in
your recipe size is discarded. Size it with `minW`/`minH` instead.

**Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Every new recipe goes into
`theme/components/index.ts`. Note the split: theme key is PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`), file is
camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does, via
`toCSSVar`. Any offline theme audit that skips that wrap passes for the wrong reason.

---

## 3. Component structure

**Placement — settled.** Design-system components live at:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/      zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/  zimmInputAction/
  organisms/  (does not exist yet)
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing: `generateRegistry.mjs` only scans that directory.

**Casing — three families, each correct in its own. Don't generalise between them.**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream exactly |

**Tier is decided by what the component's own template renders**, not by visual size. Atom =
renders no other component. Molecule = renders only atoms. Organism = renders ≥1 molecule. An icon
passed as a prop doesn't count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom); slotted children don't
count. Porting from the F2R library, the tier is already recorded as `composes: [...]` — use it.

**Styling surface — a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not
co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the
bridge: native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. F2R `.styles.ts`
files using `.zimm-*` classes are good raw material — **convert them to a recipe, don't copy the
pattern**; never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is derived output
at the *bottom* of the pipeline. Author there and you forfeit `textStyle`, the named `theme.space`
scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the theme drift guards. Not bad CSS — the
wrong end of the chain.

**Data-fetching never lives in `components/`.** A component that owns its own fetching can't be
reused where the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, story-mocked, passed from a parent).

### Two API patterns worth copying

**Encode the a11y contract in the type.** `ZimmButton` uses a discriminated union where `label` is
required in both members and doubles as `aria-label` for the icon variant — an unlabelled icon
button is *unconstructible*.

**An affordance absent from the design spec is opt-in, defaulting off** — `clearable?: boolean`.
Adding it by default put two controls in one field.

### Don't trust the generated registry's tier column

`generateRegistry.mjs:122` hardcodes tier arrays duplicating `.claude/rules/`, lists no `ui-kits`
path, and `getTier()` defaults to `4 — Feature-local`. Every design-system atom is therefore
reported as Tier 4.

---

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three distinct ways an override silently fails to take effect. Check all three before assuming
your file is live.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` rewrites
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports in the real app build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases the
package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it. So a base-path import
of a component you *have* overridden renders correctly in the app and renders the **unstyled base**
in Storybook and Vitest. Inside an override, import a sibling override by **relative path**.

**2. A relative re-export in a barrel isn't rewritten.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` is
`export {Button} from './Button'` — relative, so the resolver never sees it. Counted: **208 base
files import the barrel, 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
intercepts **nothing**, which kills the otherwise-appealing "own the primitive layer and propagate
for free" strategy.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding `footer` does not reach `/checkout`,
because base `_app/index.jsx:484` is `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}` and
`CheckoutFooter` resolves to `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a different module your
override doesn't shadow.

**The generalised check:** grep for who imports your path *and* for conditional renders of
alternates.

```bash
grep -rn "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Also worth knowing before estimating: `overrides/app/components/` contains only **seven**
directories on `develop`. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`,
`footer`, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still base despite being referenced
throughout the rules files. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's
worked example not to exist yet.

---

## 5. Figma → code

### The node-type discriminator

This is what decides whether a delta is worth chasing, and it is not a fudge factor:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Real artifacts measured:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was real, and a blanket
  "it's just cap height" rule would have dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding gave 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### Two files exist — never cross-compare

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` is the design system; `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` is composed page states.
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row: first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24 — the
design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at **402 / 1023 / 1440**. Breakpoint tokens are **768 / 860 / 1024**. The unframed
**768–1022** band was genuinely broken — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers
three iPad models in portrait. Always sweep the bands *between* frames.

### Type metrics

Measure only after the real font loads: the fallback stack renders ~13% wider. Switching to real
Futura Round moved `ORDERS & SHIPPING` 120→106px (Figma: 106, exact) and fixed two wrap bugs with
no code change. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless —
compare rendered widths instead.

### Measurement method

- Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals (the footer compares against 476, not 606,
  once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded).
- Measure `y` **relative to the component root** — Figma reports frame-relative coordinates.
- `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'`; `networkidle` never settles on a dev server.
- Dismiss the consent banner first or you measure the overlay.
- `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths, which *proves* a wrap point rather than inferring it.
- Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM mutation, one candidate at a time.
- **Mutation-test layout fixes at mobile.** Two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only because a taller
  sibling column masked them.

### A design nudge is still spec

One column's heading sat 4px right of both its own items and the other headings, with no design
reason. Correct move is to ship it and raise the question, not silently "correct" it.

---

## 6. Layout mechanics

Each of these cost real debugging time and none is obvious from a screenshot.

- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content` resolves
  to the widest unbreakable run.
- **`minHeight` + `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** Derive height from
  `lineHeight` + padding instead.
- **Inline descender leak:** a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds ~1.5–2px per row
  via the line-box strut. Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **Gap ownership.** If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, don't reproduce it as a
  sibling in a gapped flex container — you inherit a gap the design doesn't have. Give the gap to
  the heading (`marginBottom`) rather than the column.
- **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the words
  break instead.
- **Non-breaking space (` `) is the tool for controlling a wrap point** when no column cap can
  satisfy two constraints at once. Write it as the escape, never a literal NBSP byte.

---

## 7. Building against absent data

Most integrations land later; UI work isn't blocked on them. Three patterns exist and only the
first is correct.

**① Guard, then render inert but perceivable — correct.** No `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing
promises an action the app can't perform (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance) — but
**labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so assistive tech still announces that the channel exists (avoids
the 1.1.1 information loss). Switch to the live branch the moment a real destination arrives.

**② Fallback to empty string — a layout bug.** `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that keeps
its margins; measured as a ~64px void.

**③ Silent element swap — the worst.** Link→button when href validation fails gives the user a
control that looks identical and does nothing. It is the only one of the three that actively lies.

Fix ② and ③ **at the atom**, not the call site — one change covers every consumer.

**Never "render nothing."** A missing component reads as a defect to anyone reviewing the design
surface, and the links can't be tested at all.

### Guarding hrefs

Any href from CMS or fixture data goes through the shared guard. The non-obvious part: the WHATWG
URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space characters and removes tab/LF/CR **before** parsing,
so a browser reads `/\host` as `//host`. A regex without backslash and control-character handling
has a live bypass — exactly the gap that shipped:

```ts
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[�- ]+|[�- ]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[	
]/g;
const normalise = (href: string) => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```

---

## 8. Accessibility patterns

The criteria that recur, and what each actually demanded:

- **2.5.8 Target size (24px min)** — interactive controls measured 16×16 and had to become 24×24.
  On an `IconButton`, size via `minW`/`minH`; `p:` is discarded (§2).
- **2.4.7 Focus visible** — the ring belongs in the recipe's `_focusVisible`, so every consumer
  inherits it. Note **programmatic `.focus()` does not match `:focus-visible`** in Chromium — a
  test that focuses by script will report no ring even when keyboard focus shows one. Drive it with
  a real `Tab`.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must contain the visible label.
- **3.2.5 / new-window announcement** — a link that leaves the site gets
  `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its accessible name (" — opens in a new tab").
- **1.1.1 vs 2.4.4/3.2.4** — the tension behind pattern ① above: `aria-hidden` loses information,
  a fake affordance lies. Labelled-and-inert satisfies both.
- **1.4.4 Resize text** — the reason spacing and type are authored in `rem`, and the reason a
  px-authored token is not a valid substitute for a rem literal (§1).

**Interaction state belongs in the recipe** (`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`), never
in `useState`: React state is identical in a screenshot but dead until hydration, sticky on touch,
and unstylable by the theme.

---

## 9. Verification — what actually proves anything

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That single sentence explains 22 catalogued instances of a green check proving nothing. The
standard that follows: **a check must be made to fail deliberately before its pass counts.**

**Copy the non-vacuity meta-test.** `recipeGuards.test.ts` asserts its own inputs are non-empty:
*"without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green."* All four of its guards
stayed green with `components` stubbed to `{}` until that was added.

**Watch for the shape where a green test encodes a bug as correct.** `✅ contact icons are not
focusable` passed because there were no hrefs to focus — wiring them correctly *dropped* the suite
to 19/20. `✅ locale button inert` was green whether the control was inert by omission or genuinely
disabled. If a test would pass equally well on the broken and fixed versions, it asserts nothing.

**Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient.** A focus trap was mutation-tested in both wrap
directions and still let focus escape the `aria-modal` dialog when focus arrived from outside the
focusable set. Aim for orthogonal matrices where each mutation kills exactly one assertion, plus

## 1. How a value resolves

The one-way chain. Each layer may read the one above it and never the reverse:

```
theme/foundation/*.ts            source values, designer-owned — you do not add tokens here
   |
theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts   DERIVED output, emits --zimm-* onto :root — never hand-edit
   |
theme/components/<name>.ts       recipes, consuming var(--zimm-*)
   |
component JSX                    textStyle + semantic tokens only
```

### The registration reality

`theme/index.ts` registers **`borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space`,
`textStyles`** — and nothing else. `sizes`, `fontSizes`, `lineHeights`, `letterSpacings` are
absent. Measured by bundling the live theme and evaluating `css(...)(toCSSVar(theme))`:

```
padding:   'xs 0'   ->  {"padding": "xs 0"}                   // verbatim -> browser DROPS it
width:     'xl'     ->  {"width": "var(--chakra-sizes-xl)"}   // 36rem, not space.xl's 1.5rem
fontSize:  'l'      ->  {"fontSize": "l"}                     // no such key -> DROPPED
textStyle: 'footer' ->  6 resolved literals, zero var()
```

| Prop family | Resolves through | Bare scale key |
|---|---|---|
| `margin` `padding` `gap` `top/right/bottom/left` | `theme.space` (registered) | **Correct** |
| `width` `height` `boxSize` `min\|maxWidth\|Height` | `theme.sizes` (NOT registered) | **8x-112x wrong, or dropped** |
| `fontSize` `lineHeight` `letterSpacing` | `theme.fontSizes` etc. (NOT registered) | Wrong value, or dropped |

Worst measured case: `3xs` intended as 2px emits **224px**. `s`/`m`/`l` have no Chakra `sizes`
key at all, so those declarations vanish silently rather than blowing up.

**This is the single most dangerous thing in the styling layer, because the syntax is identical.**
`padding: 'xl'` is correct and `width: 'xl'` is a catastrophe. On sizing and typography props,
always the CSS var: `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`.

Live instance still in the tree: `components/header/index.tsx:302` ships `fontSize="l"`, which
emits nothing.

### textStyle can never emit a var — and what that means

`zimmTokens.ts` imports *from* `typography.ts`, so the reverse would be a circular import.
`textStyle` therefore always expands to resolved literals at build time. **This is correct
behaviour, not a defect** — and it means roughly **85% of what an emitted-CSS audit flags as
"raw literals" is `textStyle` working as designed.**

**So the real invariant is single-sourcing, not `var()` syntax.** The question to ask of any value
is *"is this typed more than once?"* — not *"is this a `var()`?"* An audit built on syntax
generates mostly noise.

### Value equality is not token equality

**[CORRECTED]** Three constants were once flagged as "mirrors" duplicating existing tokens.
**All three were false positives.** Rewriting `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` to `var(--zimm-scale-1200)`
would have been a **WCAG 1.4.4 regression** — that token is authored in **px**, which does not
scale under zoom — plus a numeric-alias violation, and there is no valid named token in the gap
(the scale jumps 2.5rem -> 4rem).

Before "fixing" any apparent duplicate, gate it on three checks:

1. **Same unit?** rem and px are not interchangeable; rem is required wherever text or spacing
   must scale under zoom.
2. **Same semantic scale?** A coincidental numeric match is not a relationship.
3. **Is the target a permitted token?** `--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases are class-only; naming
   one from a recipe is itself a violation.

Known numeric-alias violations in the tree: `listMenu.ts:17,33,65,84` and `header.ts:59`. Match
them with `var\(--zimm-scale-[0-9]+\)` — a bare `[0-9]` also matches `3xs` and inflates the count.

### Units

`rem` for anything that must scale with root font size or zoom (type, spacing). `px` only for
hairline geometry that must *not* scale — border widths, focus-ring offsets. `em` only for
breakpoints.

## 2. Chakra behaviours that fail silently

**`extendTheme` deep-merges — namespace every recipe.** SFCC ships its own `Footer` recipe. Naming
ours `Footer` merged into it: copyright rendered 14px instead of 10px and the subscribe heading
lost its 24px gap. The mechanism is ordering — an existing key is overwritten *in place*, a **new**
key is appended **last**, so your `margin: 0` shorthand lands after the base's `marginBottom` and
wipes it. Hence `ZimmFooter`, `ZimmTextInput`, `ZimmNavItem`.

**A recipe unit test cannot catch this.** In isolation Chakra emitted the correct order; the
collision only appears merged. Intentional merges are allowlisted in `recipeGuards.test.ts`:
`Button`, `Header`, `ListMenu`.

**Compound values are never tokenised.** Chakra resolves a token only as the *entire* value.
`padding: 'xs 0'` ships verbatim and the browser discards the declaration. Use axis props.

**Shorthand after longhand resets it.** `padding: 0` declared after `paddingBlock` silently kills
it. Use `paddingInline`.

**`IconButton` hard-sets `padding: "0"` as a style prop**, merged *after* `__css`, so a `p:` in
your recipe size is discarded. Size it with `minW`/`minH` instead.

**Register the recipe or destructuring throws at runtime.** Every new recipe goes into
`theme/components/index.ts`. Note the split: theme key is PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`), file is
camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**`extendTheme` does not populate `theme.__cssMap`** — only `ChakraProvider` does, via `toCSSVar`.
Any offline theme audit that skips that wrap passes for the wrong reason.

## 3. Component structure

**Placement — settled.** Design-system components live at:

```
overrides/app/components/ui-kits/
  atoms/      zimmButton/  zimmIcon/  zimmLogo/  zimmNavItem/  zimmTextInput/
  molecules/  zimmInputAction/
  organisms/  (does not exist yet)
```

Being under `components/` is load-bearing: `generateRegistry.mjs` only scans that directory.

**Casing — three families, each correct in its own. Do not generalise between them.**

| Family | Casing | Why |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path |
| ui-kit component | `zimmButton/` camelCase | Zimmermann-authored — the default |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream exactly |

**Tier is decided by what the component's own template renders**, not by visual size. Atom =
renders no other component. Molecule = renders only atoms. Organism = renders at least one
molecule. An icon passed as a prop does not count (`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom); slotted
children do not count. Porting from the F2R library, the tier is already recorded as
`composes: [...]` — use it.

**Styling surface — a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class, not
co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is the
bridge: native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. F2R `.styles.ts`
files using `.zimm-*` classes are good raw material — **convert them to a recipe, do not copy the
pattern**; never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is derived output
at the *bottom* of the pipeline. Author there and you forfeit `textStyle`, the named `theme.space`
scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the theme drift guards. Not bad CSS — the
wrong end of the chain.

**Data-fetching never lives in `components/`.** A component that owns its own fetching cannot be
reused where the data arrives differently (SSR-prefetched, story-mocked, passed from a parent).

### Two API patterns worth copying

**Encode the a11y contract in the type.** `ZimmButton` uses a discriminated union where `label` is
required in both members and doubles as `aria-label` for the icon variant — an unlabelled icon
button is *unconstructible*.

**An affordance absent from the design spec is opt-in, defaulting off** — `clearable?: boolean`.
Adding it by default put two controls in one field.

## 4. What an override actually intercepts

Three distinct ways an override silently fails to take effect. Check all three before assuming
your file is live.

**1. The resolver is webpack-only.** `ccExtensibility` rewrites
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports in the real app build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases the
package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` does not touch it. So a base-path import
of a component you *have* overridden renders correctly in the app and renders the **unstyled base**
in Storybook and Vitest. Inside an override, import a sibling override by **relative path**.

**2. A relative re-export in a barrel is not rewritten.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` is
`export {Button} from './Button'` — relative, so the resolver never sees it. Counted: **208 base
files import the barrel, 0 import `shared/ui/Button`.** Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
intercepts **nothing**, which kills the otherwise-appealing "own the primitive layer and propagate
for free" strategy.

**3. A conditional render of an alternate module.** Overriding `footer` does not reach `/checkout`,
because base `_app/index.jsx:484` is `{!isCheckout ? <Footer /> : <CheckoutFooter />}` and
`CheckoutFooter` resolves to `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer` — a different module your
override does not shadow.

**The generalised check:** grep for who imports your path *and* for conditional renders of
alternates.

```bash
grep -rn "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" \
  node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/
```

Also worth knowing before estimating: `overrides/app/components/` contains only **seven**
directories on `develop`. `product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`,

throughout the rules files. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's
worked example not to exist yet.

## 5. Figma to code

### The node-type discriminator

This is what decides whether a delta is worth chasing, and it is not a fudge factor:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Real artifacts measured:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was real, and a blanket
  "it is just cap height" rule would have dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is
a defect. Three contact items all at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding gave 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### Two files exist — never cross-compare

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` is the design system; `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` is composed page states.
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row: first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320x44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308x59, with a compensating gap change 40->24 — the
design **repositions**, it does not reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed
intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at **402 / 1023 / 1440**. Breakpoint tokens are **768 / 860 / 1024**. The unframed
**768-1022** band was genuinely broken — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers
three iPad models in portrait. Always sweep the bands *between* frames.

### Type metrics

Measure only after the real font loads: the fallback stack renders ~13% wider. Switching to real
Futura Round moved `ORDERS & SHIPPING` 120->106px (Figma: 106, exact) and fixed two wrap bugs with
no code change. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless —
compare rendered widths instead.

### Measurement method

- Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals (the footer compares against 476, not 606,
  once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded).
- Measure `y` **relative to the component root** — Figma reports frame-relative coordinates.
- `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'`; `networkidle` never settles on a dev server.
- Dismiss the consent banner first or you measure the overlay.
- `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths, which *proves* a wrap point rather than
  inferring it.
- Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM mutation, one candidate at a time.
- **Mutation-test layout fixes at mobile.** Two fixes read as delta-0 at 1440 only because a
  taller sibling column masked them.

### A design nudge is still spec

One column's heading sat 4px right of both its own items and the other headings, with no design
reason. Correct move is to ship it and raise the question, not silently "correct" it.

## 6. Layout mechanics

Each of these cost real debugging time and none is obvious from a screenshot.

- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content` resolves
  to the widest unbreakable run.
- **`minHeight` + `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** Derive height from
  `lineHeight` + padding instead.
- **Inline descender leak:** a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds ~1.5-2px per row
  via the line-box strut. Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **Gap ownership.** If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, do not reproduce it as
  a sibling in a gapped flex container — you inherit a gap the design does not have. Give the gap
  to the heading (`marginBottom`) rather than the column.
- **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the words
  break instead.
- **A non-breaking space is the tool for controlling a wrap point** when no column cap can satisfy
  two constraints at once. Always write it as the escape ` `, never as a literal NBSP byte.

## 7. Building against absent data

Most integrations land later; UI work is not blocked on them. Three patterns exist and only the
first is correct.

**(1) Guard, then render inert but perceivable — correct.** No `href`, no `tabIndex`, so nothing
promises an action the app cannot perform (avoids the WCAG 2.4.4 / 3.2.4 false affordance) — but
**labelled, not `aria-hidden`**, so assistive tech still announces that the channel exists (avoids
the 1.1.1 information loss). Switch to the live branch the moment a real destination arrives.

**(2) Fallback to empty string — a layout bug.** `heading ?? ''` renders an empty element that
keeps its margins; measured as a ~64px void.

**(3) Silent element swap — the worst.** Link-to-button when href validation fails gives the user a
control that looks identical and does nothing. It is the only one of the three that actively lies.

Fix (2) and (3) **at the atom**, not the call site — one change covers every consumer.

**Never "render nothing."** A missing component reads as a defect to anyone reviewing the design
surface, and the links cannot be tested at all.

### Guarding hrefs

Any href from CMS or fixture data goes through the shared guard. The non-obvious part: the WHATWG
URL parser strips leading/trailing C0-or-space characters and removes tab/LF/CR **before** parsing,
so a browser reads a backslash-prefixed path as a protocol-relative URL. A regex without backslash
and control-character handling has a live bypass — exactly the gap that shipped:

```ts

const TAB_LF_CR = /[

/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
const normalise = (href: string) => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```

## 8. Accessibility patterns

The criteria that recur, and what each actually demanded:

- **2.5.8 Target size (24px min)** — interactive controls measured 16x16 and had to become 24x24.
  On an `IconButton`, size via `minW`/`minH`; `p:` is discarded (section 2).
- **2.4.7 Focus visible** — the ring belongs in the recipe's `_focusVisible`, so every consumer
  inherits it. Note **programmatic `.focus()` does not match `:focus-visible`** in Chromium — a
  test that focuses by script reports no ring even when keyboard focus shows one. Drive it with a
  real `Tab`.
- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must contain the visible label.
- **3.2.5 / new-window announcement** — a link that leaves the site gets
  `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and a suffix in its accessible name (" - opens in a new tab").
- **1.1.1 vs 2.4.4/3.2.4** — the tension behind pattern (1) above: `aria-hidden` loses
  information, a fake affordance lies. Labelled-and-inert satisfies both.
- **1.4.4 Resize text** — the reason spacing and type are authored in `rem`, and the reason a
  px-authored token is not a valid substitute for a rem literal (section 1).

**Interaction state belongs in the recipe** (`_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`), never
in `useState`: React state is identical in a screenshot but dead until hydration, sticky on touch,
and unstylable by the theme.

### The node-type discriminator

This decides whether a delta is worth chasing, and it is not a fudge factor:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`,
  `text-box-edge: cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts:
  "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs 18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box** and are **directly comparable**, so a delta there
  is a genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was real; a blanket
  "it is just cap height" rule would have dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all at +7 after every real cause was removed was the heading's cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` plus
4.5px padding gave 24/24/24/24/38 = 134, exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

### Two files exist, so never cross-compare

`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` is the design system; `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` is composed page states.
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row: first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320x44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308x59, with a compensating gap change 40 to 24 —
the design **repositions**, it does not reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed
intended growth when the 68px padded box was already correct.

### Frames are not breakpoints

Frames exist at **402 / 1023 / 1440**; breakpoint tokens are **768 / 860 / 1024**. The unframed
**768-1022** band was genuinely broken — 18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels — and covers
three iPad models in portrait. Always sweep the bands *between* frames.

### Type metrics

Measure only after the real font loads: the fallback stack renders about 13% wider. Switching to
real Futura Round moved `ORDERS & SHIPPING` from 120 to 106px (Figma: 106, exact) and fixed two
wrap bugs with no code change. `document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and
is useless — compare rendered widths instead.

### Measurement method

- Subtract non-component bands before comparing totals (the footer compares against 476, not 606,
  once the `Disclaimer` band is excluded).
- Measure `y` **relative to the component root**; Figma reports frame-relative coordinates.
- `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` — `networkidle` never settles on a dev server.
- Dismiss the consent banner first or you measure the overlay.
- `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths, which *proves* a wrap point rather than inferring

- Isolate causes by cumulative in-DOM mutation, one candidate at a time.
- **Mutation-test layout fixes at mobile.** Two fixes read as zero delta at 1440 only because a
  taller sibling column masked them.

### A design nudge is still spec

One column's heading sat 4px right of both its own items and the other headings, with no design
reason. Ship it and raise the question; do not silently "correct" it.

## 6. Layout mechanics

Each cost real debugging time and none is obvious from a screenshot.

- **A wrapped element takes available width, not its longest line.** `width: min-content` resolves
  to the widest unbreakable run.
- **`minHeight` plus `align-items: center` loses leading when content wraps.** Derive height from
  `lineHeight` plus padding instead.
- **Inline descender leak:** a block `<li>` wrapping an `inline-flex` `<a>` adds roughly 1.5-2px per
  row via the line-box strut. Fix with `display: flex` on the `<li>`.
- **Gap ownership.** If the design nests a group inside a stack with no gap, do not reproduce it as
  a sibling in a gapped flex container — you inherit a gap the design does not have. Give the gap to
  the heading (`marginBottom`) rather than the column.
- **`flexWrap: nowrap` prevents breaking, not shrinking.** The row refuses to break, so the words
  break instead.

## 8. Accessibility patterns

The criteria that recur, and what each actually demanded:

- **2.5.8 Target size (24px min)** — controls measured 16x16 and had to become 24x24. On an

- **2.5.3 Label in name** — the accessible name must contain the visible label.
- **3.2.5, new-window announcement** — a link leaving the site gets `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and
  a suffix in its accessible name.

  fake affordance lies. Labelled-and-inert satisfies both.
- **1.4.4 Resize text** — why spacing and type are authored in `rem`, and why a px-authored token

in `useState`. React state looks identical in a screenshot but is dead until hydration, sticky on

### The integrity principle

> The verification instrument was built from the same belief as the thing it verified, and was
> never made to fail on purpose.

That one sentence explains 22 catalogued instances of a green check proving nothing. The standard
that follows: **a check must be made to fail deliberately before its pass counts.**

**Copy the non-vacuity meta-test.** `recipeGuards.test.ts` asserts its own inputs are non-empty —
*"without this, deleting `components` would turn the whole file green."* All four of its guards
stayed green with `components` stubbed to an empty object until that was added.

**Watch for a green test that encodes a bug as correct.** "contact icons are not focusable" passed
because there were no hrefs to focus; wiring them correctly *dropped* the suite to 19/20. "locale
button inert" was green whether the control was inert by omission or genuinely disabled. If a test
would pass equally on the broken and the fixed version, it asserts nothing.

**Mutation testing is necessary but not sufficient.** A focus trap was mutation-tested in both wrap
directions and still let focus escape the `aria-modal` dialog when focus arrived from outside the
focusable set. Aim for orthogonal matrices where each mutation kills exactly one assertion, plus
deliberate false-positive controls.

- **`test-storybook` needs a *built* Storybook.** Dev-server runs made four mutation results

- **Vitest does not run `play` functions.** A story `play` is not unit coverage.

**[CORRECTED] a11y IS gated.** The widely-repeated conclusion that it was not ("no
`.storybook/test-runner.js`") was Storybook 8 knowledge. With what is installed —

purpose, so it is unproven rather than absent.

parsing, so a browser reads a backslash-prefixed path as protocol-relative. A regex without
backslash and control-character handling has a live bypass — exactly the gap that shipped. Normalise
first, then test:

```ts
/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
const normalise = (href: string) =>
  href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
```

A space-prefixed path stays allowed on purpose: a space is percent-encoded by the browser and
--- nbsp bullet ---
294:- **A non-breaking space is the tool for controlling a wrap point** when no column cap can satisfy
295-  two constraints at once. Always write it as the escape `\u00A0`, never as a literal NBSP
296-  byte — a literal one is invisible in review and in a diff.

Done. **`~/Desktop/uiBuild-knowledge.md`** — 457 lines, ten sections, no role or process material in it.

## What's in it

How a value resolves (the derivation chain and the registration reality) · Chakra behaviours that fail silently · component structure · what an override actually intercepts · Figma to code · layout mechanics · building against absent data · accessibility patterns · verification · signposts in the repo that point at nothing.

Every claim was re-verified against the installed toolchain rather than carried over from where it was first learned. That mattered more than expected — **four widely-repeated conclusions from the footer build were wrong**, and they're marked `[CORRECTED]` in place:

- **a11y *is* gated.** The session concluded four separate times that it wasn't, on the grounds that there's no `.storybook/test-runner.js`. That was Storybook 8 knowledge. With `@storybook/test-runner@0.24.4` the runner reads `parameters.a11y.test` and rejects on `"error"`, which `preview.tsx` sets. No `test-runner.js` needed — and believing otherwise is how that block gets deleted.
- **Component structure is decided**, not unsettled: `ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/`, theme recipe always.
- **Figma's cap-height box applies to text nodes only.** Frames and instances report real boxes and *are* comparable, so "it's just cap height" would have dismissed a genuine 44/59-vs-45/68 defect.
- **Value equality is not token equality.** All three constants flagged as duplicate "mirrors" were false positives, and the proposed fix would have been a WCAG 1.4.4 regression — px token substituted for a rem literal.

Three of those four had already gone into my memory from the earlier reads, so I've corrected them there too, plus added one on authorisation and scope discipline from the process agent. Memory now stands at 37 entries.

## Two things outside the document

**PR #59's required checks are all `skipping` right now.** `detect-changes` uses `since_last_remote_commit: true`, and the final push (`ec9d161`) touched only the registry and its generator — outside every allow-list. So a 64-commit, ~5,000-line PR is sitting merge-eligible with zero test evidence on its head SHA. Worth a no-op commit to re-trigger before anyone approves.

**`provisional-token-audit.md` is still recoverable** — the full 15,307-character write from 19 Aug is in the transcript. I haven't restored it, since you cleared the Desktop deliberately. `fedBuild-manual.md` and `fedLead-playbook.md` are intact in `~/Downloads/`.

One open governance item I'll flag rather than resolve: AGENTS.md #8 lists `.storybook/` as flatly frozen while the playbook reads the verified-approver exception as applying. This branch acted on the second reading and CodeRabbit flagged it Major; only the citation got fixed, never the interpretation. That's a real conflict between two Tier 1 sources, and it needs a ruling rather than another workaround.

- `textStyle` can never emit a `var()` (circular import would result); expands to resolved literals — so ~85% of "raw literal" findings in a CSS audit is textStyle working correctly

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
```

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

# Tagging & Environment Promotion

How releases are versioned, tagged, and promoted through the environments. This is the
day-to-day companion to the branch rules in [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) (Branch Rules) and the
supervised-release flow in [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) —
this file covers **tags and promotion**, those cover **branches**.

---

## Tag taxonomy

Every deployable version is an **immutable, annotated git tag**. The **tag-promoted** tiers
(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`) deploy a specific tag — never "whatever's on a branch right
now." (The continuous tiers are the exception: `dev` and `sit` deploy commit refs, and Test also
takes a branch ref for on-demand quick looks — see the Environment model below.)

| Pattern | Meaning | Example | Cut from | Who |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` | Release candidate — a stabilising snapshot, cheap to iterate | `v0.1.0-rc.2` | a commit on `release/vX.Y.Z` | **any developer** |
| `vX.Y.Z` | Final release — the exact candidate that passed every gate | `v0.1.0` | the `release/vX.Y.Z` commit merged to `main` | **tier-1-approver only** |
| `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N` | Emergency fix candidate, outside the normal train | `v0.1.1-hotfix.1` | a commit on `hotfix/vX.Y.Z` | **tier-1-approver only** |

**Versioning:**
- **MAJOR** locked at `0` pre-launch (SemVer reserves `0.y.z` for initial development). `v1.0.0`
  is reserved for **go-live**; MAJOR reverts to its normal rare-breaking-change meaning after.
- **MINOR** bumps once per sprint, when a new `release/vX.Y.Z` branch is cut — sprint 1 = `v0.1.0`,
  sprint 2 = `v0.2.0`.
- **PATCH** = bug-fix-only release against an already-shipped `MAJOR.MINOR` (e.g. a hotfix after
  `v0.1.0` → `v0.1.1`).
- The `-rc.N` counter is a plain incrementing number, **not** an environment reference — it counts
  candidate builds, not deployments. The same `v0.1.0-rc.1` can be deployed (and re-deployed) to
  Test on demand; which environment ran which candidate is tracked via each `deploy-*.yml`'s Actions
  run history, not the tag name.
- The dot in `-rc.N` matters: SemVer compares `rc.10 > rc.2` numerically only as dot-separated
  fields; `rc10`/`rc2` would sort alphabetically (wrong). This is exactly what the version-guard
  relies on.

Non-`v*` tags are a separate namespace and unaffected by any of this: `sprint/{N}/{date}` (sprint
rollover, auto-cut by `deploy-dev.yml`) and any `sit/deploy/*` refs.

---

## Cutting a tag

Tags are cut with a **tag-only push** — a raw annotated `git tag`, then pushing the tag alone. We
deliberately avoid `npm version`: it creates a local `package.json`-bump *commit* alongside the tag,
and pushing that commit to the release branch is blocked by `release/**` branch protection
(`isAdminEnforced`, no bypass). Pushing only the tag sidesteps this — a tag push is not a branch
push. **Consequence:** `package.json`'s `version` field does not auto-track each candidate — it is
bumped once, deliberately, at the final-release PR.

**Release candidate (any developer):**

```bash
git checkout release/v0.1.0 && git pull --ff-only   # fail rather than tag a local merge commit
git tag -a v0.1.0-rc.0 -m "Release candidate v0.1.0-rc.0"
git push origin v0.1.0-rc.0           # tag only — NOT a branch push
gh workflow run deploy-test.yml -f ref=v0.1.0-rc.0
```

- Always **annotated** (`-a -m`) — the tagger identity, timestamp, and message live in the tag
  object (`git show v0.1.0-rc.0`). Never lightweight.
- A tag push is not a branch push, so branch protection doesn't block it.

**Final release (tier-1-approver only):** cut `vX.Y.Z` on the release-branch commit being merged to
`main`, then promote it up through `uat` → `staging` → `prod`. Run [`/generate-changelog`](../skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md)
at this point to produce the GitHub Release.

**Rollback.** The downgrade guard (see below) deliberately blocks deploying an older tag, so a
rollback takes one of two authorised paths:

- **Emergency (fastest) — re-activate the previous bundle in Managed Runtime**, outside the deploy
  pipeline (the rollback procedure in the Environment Topology doc). This does not run the guard, so
  afterwards re-record the baseline so it doesn't treat a superseded tag as live:
  `node scripts/versionGuard.mjs record prod v0.1.0`.
- **Controlled — pipeline rollback with the guard override.** Redeploy the known-good tag with
  `rollback=true`; the guard's downgrade check is skipped (the run logs the skip for audit) and
  `record` still runs, so the rolled-back tag becomes the new live baseline:
  `gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f ref=v0.1.0 -f rollback=true`. Because this bypasses the guard,
  its only human gate is the environment's **required reviewers** — so `prod` (and `staging`/`uat`)
  must have required reviewers with "prevent self-review" configured. **Prerequisite: until that is
  set, `rollback=true` is not gated.**

---

## Enforcement — what actually holds the line

On this org's GitHub **`team`** plan, ruleset *metadata* rules (`tag_name_pattern`) are
Enterprise-only and silently **inert** — a malformed `v*` tag is not blocked at push time by a
ruleset. Naming is enforced by the hook and workflow below, not the rulesets. Three layers, in
order of reliability:

1. **Pre-push hook** ([.husky/pre-push](../../.husky/pre-push) → [scripts/hooks/pre-push](../../scripts/hooks/pre-push))
   — *best-effort prevention*. Rejects a malformed `v*` tag before it leaves the developer's machine
   — the earliest catch, but bypassable (`git push --no-verify`, or a checkout without the hook
   installed), so not a hard guarantee. Allowed: `vX.Y.Z-rc.N`, `vX.Y.Z`, `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`.
   Non-`v*` tags and branch pushes pass through untouched.
2. **`tag-validate.yml`** ([.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml](../../.github/workflows/tag-validate.yml))
   — *detection*. Fails if a malformed `v*` tag lands on the remote (post-hoc alert, not a block).
3. **GitHub Rulesets** `tag-rc` (id 20487306) + `tag-release` (id 20487243) — enforce what core rules
   *can* on the `team` plan: **immutability** (`update` + `deletion` restricted) and **tier-1-only
   final tags** (`creation` restricted on `tag-release`, bypass = `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`).
   Their `tag_name_pattern` rules (`^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` and `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-hotfix\.\d+)?$`)
   are **kept but inert on `team`** — they self-activate if the org ever upgrades to Enterprise.

GitHub ruleset objects have no free-text description field, so the "inert on team" caveat can't
live on the ruleset itself — this section is its canonical record. The rulesets may optionally be
renamed in Settings → Rules to append " — naming inert on team plan" for an at-a-glance signal.

---

## Environment model — two categories

| Category | Environments | How it deploys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Continuous / auto** | `dev`, `sit` | No human-picked tag. `dev` auto-deploys every `develop` merge; `sit` deploys the gate's commit via `workflow_run` off the SIT Gate on `release/**`. |
| **Tag-promoted / deliberate** | `test`, `uat`, `staging`, `prod` | `workflow_dispatch` with a specific tag `ref`. Each can sit on a different tag simultaneously, decoupling their cadences. |

**SIT stays branch/gate-driven** — its `workflow_run` trigger off the SIT Gate on `release/**` is
unchanged. This is an intentional exception to "every environment sits on a named tag": SIT is a
continuous auto-integration tier, the same category as `dev`, not a deliberate pinned-promotion
tier. Using tags is not the same as being triggered by a tag — tags and Releases still exist and are
visible; SIT simply auto-refreshes.

**Environment names are the real GitHub Environment names** — `dev / test / sit / uat / staging /
prod`. Tooling must key off these, not the workflow-file suffix: `deploy-stg.yml` binds
`environment: staging` (the `stg`≠`staging` mismatch already caused a bug once).

---

## Downgrade protection (version-guard)

[scripts/versionGuard.mjs](../../scripts/versionGuard.mjs), wired into the four tag-promoted
`deploy-*.yml` workflows:

- **`check <env> <ref>`** runs *before* the push: reads the environment's last recorded deployed tag
  and **blocks** if `ref` is semver-older (`semver.lt`). Skips non-`v*` refs, allows the first-ever
  deploy, and **fails closed** on any lookup/parse error.
- **`record <env> <ref>`** runs *after* a successful push: stamps the deployed tag as an explicit
  GitHub Deployment (the auto-created Deployment records the *trigger* ref, not the deployed tag, so
  we record it ourselves and read it back).
- **`dev` and `sit` are excluded** — they have no human-picked `ref` to compare (consistent with the
  two-category model above).
- Guard/record key off the **GitHub Environment name** (`stg`→`staging`).

---

## The Test gate

`deploy-test.yml` runs **deploy-then-gate**: it deploys first (Test is the fast, disposable
quick-look tier), then a post-deploy gate verifies the same build. The run's overall pass/fail is the
**"safe to promote to SIT"** signal.

- **`bundle-size`** — `npm run test:max-file-size`, enforcing the `package.json` budgets
  (`main.js` ≤ 180 kB, `vendor.js` ≤ 550 kB). Bundle-size is cheap, deterministic, and mobile
  page-speed is a top project priority, so bloat is caught at the earliest deployed tier.
- **P0 Playwright** — attaches to the same gate once a `*.p0.spec` exists (Lead QA, gherkin-first);
  it targets the Test storefront via the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` variable.

This intentionally differs from SIT's **gate-then-deploy** (`digital-sit.yml`), which can hang a
pre-check on a `release/**` push event that Test doesn't have.

---

# Styling an Override Component

How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
companion.

---

## The hierarchy — reach for these in order

1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
2. **Semantic colour/spacing token strings** — `color="text.default"`, `bg="background.02"`,
   `spacing="m"`, `padding={{ base: 'm', md: 'xl' }}`. These resolve through
   `theme.colors`/`theme.space` (both registered — see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment
   for which foundation scales are and aren't registered, and why).
3. **A component's own theme config** (`theme/components/<name>.ts`) for anything that
   needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
   "Component-local tokens" below. For an interactive component with existing Chakra
   support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme config is the single source of truth —
   see "One canonical styling surface per component type" below.
4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.

**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
instead. The one standing exception is `button.ts`'s provisional height/padding
constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
sign-off — see Units below. Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before opening
a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`
— it greps for exactly this. It is not wired into CI yet — that's a reasonable next
step once someone owns triaging its false positives (hairline px is expected and
not a bug; see below).

## Units

- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
  comment for traceability.
- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `button.ts` that are
  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.

## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy

`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
if only one of them is ever typed.

`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.

## One canonical styling surface per component type

Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its
`theme/components/<name>.ts` config, consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
with the real theme config over time. `button.ts` is the single source of truth for
button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
for any button, not a class.

`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
there's no interactive state to lose.

## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component

If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import, which is correct for that file).

The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
override and isn't.

**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.

An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.

## Component-local tokens

When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference it **by name** in the theme config
(`marginBottom: 'xs'`, not `marginBottom: 2` or `marginBottom: '0.5rem'`) — Chakra
resolves named scale keys against the registered `theme.space` automatically. See
`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` for the pattern: both re-express
values the base SFCC theme already had as anonymous Chakra numerics (`marginBottom: 2`)
using our named scale instead, at the same responsive steps (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs',
'xs']` instead of `[1, 1, 2, 2]`) — same computed output, now traceable to a brand
token.

When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
`header.ts`/`button.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.

## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)

If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies — their default exports are
kept API-compatible; brand styling for them lives in their `theme/components/*.ts`
config instead of a named-export split, since token-driven theming doesn't require a
second export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

---

## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)

- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
- `button.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `button.ts`,
  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.

## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)

- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

   - Existing PDP-adjacent component overrides: overrides/app/components/image-gallery/, swatch-group/, display-price/, product-tile/, product-item/, recommended-products/, product-view/ (if present), quantity-picker. For each: does an override exist, and does it have a theme recipe in overrides/app/theme/components/?

2. THE COMPONENT STRUCTURE CONVENTION. The settled convention in this repo is:
   overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx
   with styling ALWAYS via a theme recipe in overrides/app/theme/components/, registered in that folder's index.ts.
   - List what actually exists under overrides/app/components/ui-kits/ today (I believe only a handful of directories exist).
   - Report the naming families in play so they are not confused: SFCC override dirs are kebab-case (product-tile/), ui-kit components are camelCase (zimmButton/), shared/ui primitives are PascalCase (Button/).
   - Read .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md and any .claude/rules/overrides.md for the authoritative statement, and report where the branch's code diverges.

3. THE COMPONENT REGISTRY. There is a `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` and related registry work (recently active on branch feature/f2r-component-registry, 31 commits ahead). Determine:

   - Whether the registry exists on THIS branch or only on the f2r branch — i.e. whether it is a dependency we would be building against something not yet merged to develop.

4. THREE OVERRIDE INTERCEPT TRAPS — verify whether any apply to the PDP work:
   a. The `ccExtensibility` resolver that redirects `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to overrides/ runs ONLY in the real webpack build. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to node_modules and vitest.config.ts does not touch it. So importing an ALREADY-OVERRIDDEN component by its base path renders/tests the UNSTYLED BASE version in Storybook and Vitest while working correctly in the app. Grep the PDP code for base-path imports of components that have local overrides.

Check overrides/app/components/shared/ui/ — if the base barrel re-exports './Button' relatively and 208 base files import the barrel rather than the deep path, then overriding shared/ui/<Name> intercepts nothing. Verify whether the PDP work depends on this.
   c. Conditional render of an alternate module: e.g. base _app/index.jsx renders <CheckoutFooter/> instead of <Footer/> on checkout, so overriding footer does not reach /checkout. Check whether PDP has any equivalent conditional-swap that would bypass an override.

5. DATA LAYER. The rule is that components under overrides/app/components/ receive data as props and do NOT call data-fetching hooks; fetching belongs in overrides/app/pages/. Report how product data currently reaches the PDP (which hook, in which file) and what shape it is, so new components can be typed against it. Note the project rule: no mocking in production paths, all data from live Commerce Cloud API via @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react.

**The AC exists but is easy to miss** — it's in the `Acceptance Criteria` custom field (`customfield_10231`), not the description. Six Given/When/Then items: name, price (single full price, storefront currency), description, style code, model copy (+ its negative case: no empty placeholder), and breadcrumb (beneath the product pictures, `HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]`, nodes navigate to category). Two extra styling ACs live in standalone Tasks **SFCC-732/733** (both `To Do`), citing Figma node **5804-170721**.

**IN SCOPE:** name · full price · description · "Model is…" copy (optional) · style code · breadcrumb. Note the description's In Scope list has a literally empty first bullet — an authoring artifact, not a hidden requirement.

### Four things that matter most for taking this over

1. **Model copy uses the wrong attribute.** SFCC-26 (the blocking attribute story) defines `modelFit` *specifically* for the PDP model line, and `sizeFit` for the Size & Fit tab (SFCC-102, out of scope). Jasmijn's comments confirm `modelFit` was created deliberately for this. The branch instead regex-scrapes `<li>Model is…</li>` out of `c_sizeFit` — the pre-decision Magento behaviour, English-only across 11 locales. Needs a human decision, not a silent fix.

2. **Two live tickets claim the same scope.** **SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content`** (epic SFCC-2, Ready For Review) says it covers "product name, description, model description, style code" — verbatim SFCC-89. Confluence 04.71 says Level 2 page stories must *not* repeat Level 1 component build detail. The component build arguably belongs to SFCC-737; layout in `product-detail/index.tsx` arguably belongs to **SFCC-723 `pdp/hero`**.

3. **Breadcrumb is cross-squad contested.** **SFCC-578 "SEO — Breadcrumb Component (PLP & PDP)"** is Squad-B, epic SFCC-22, still To Do, describing the same component — and SFCC-573/570 depend on it. The branch already built it, without the SEO obligations.

4. **Governance blockers on the branch:** `package.json` adds `isomorphic-dompurify` — **Tier 1 frozen file + Hard Rule #7** (no packages without integration approval), no approval recorded. Plus `routes.tsx` and `theme/components/` (both Tier 2) — that's a multi-tier change, tripping Hard Rule #10.

**Other blockers:** SFCC-26 is "Ready to **deploy** to UAT" and 3 E2E tests are skipped "pending sandbox product provisioning" — the AC is unproven against real data. Subtask **SFCC-712 Test Case Execution is To Do**. Confluence 04.72 puts PDP stories "ready for development" at **Aug 24** (today is 22nd) and 04.7 lists Product Content as *"Done, minor update required"* — the design isn't locked.

**Doc conflicts:** `.docs/prd/pdp.md` marks PRD-023/PRD-025 as confirmed, but Confluence 04.1.8 has both **struck through / out of scope** — the local mirror is stale. `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` still says "Sprint 0 in progress" and dates Sprint 3 as 27 Jul–7 Aug vs Jira's 10–24 Aug; don't rely on it. `projectState.md` has no record of this work at all. `.docs/prd/pdp.md` is otherwise consistent with the ticket on everything in scope.

Also worth a quick fix: `styleCode` reads `product.id`, but SFCC-26 says the style code is the *master* ID (`styleNumber`) — this becomes a real bug the moment SFCC-91 introduces colour-variant routing. And SFCC-732/733 assert `.product-name` / `.product-price` selectors the component doesn't expose (values match, selectors don't) — they'll fail at QA as written.</result>

content.text:
Confirmed, and it's worse than a naming issue: `isomorphic-dompurify@^3.19.0` was added as a **production** dependency, and the lockfile shows the install flipped a chain of `jsdom`-related packages (`@asamuzakjp/*`, and others) from `dev: true` into the production tree. ## Requirements agent — what came back **SFCC-89** is a 5-point Story in Sprint 3, status *Code Review*, assigned to Jhoan, reported by Jasmijn, due 17 Aug (five days ago). Parent epic SFCC-5 (PDP) — a Level 2 *page* epic. The acceptance criteria aren't in the description — they're in a custom field, which is easy to miss. Six Given/When/Then items: product name, single full price in storefront currency, description, style code, "Model is…" copy including its negative case, and the breadcrumb beneath the product images. Two further styling ACs sit in separate Tasks, SFCC-732/733, both still To Do. ### Four things that need your call **1. Scope collision — three tickets claim this work.** SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content` (Ready For Review) describes "product name, description, model description, style code" — verbatim SFCC-89. SFCC-723 `pdp/hero` arguably owns the layout. And the breadcrumb is described by **SFCC-578 "SEO — Breadcrumb Component (PLP & PDP)"**, which is *Squad B*, still To Do, with SFCC-573/570 depending on it. The branch has already built the breadcrumb, without the SEO obligations attached to it. **2. The model copy reads the wrong attribute.** SFCC-26 deliberately created `modelFit` for exactly this PDP line, with `sizeFit` reserved for the Size & Fit tab (SFCC-102, out of scope). Jasmijn's comments confirm that was intentional. The branch instead regex-scrapes `
  • Model is…
    • ` out of `c_sizeFit` — the old Magento behaviour, and English-only across 11 locales. **3. `isomorphic-dompurify` needs integration-team approval.** Hard Rule #7, and `package.json` is Tier 1 frozen. Beyond the process point, pulling jsdom into the production tree against a ≤180 kB `main.js` / ≤550 kB `vendor.js` budget and a 2s p75 mobile LCP target deserves a real look. Combined with Tier 2 edits to `routes.tsx` and `theme/components/`, this is also a multi-tier change — Hard Rule #10. **4. Style code reads `product.id`,** but SFCC-26 defines it as the *master* ID. That's latent until SFCC-91 adds colour-variant routing, then it silently shows the wrong code. Also: `.docs/prd/pdp.md` marks PRD-023/PRD-025 confirmed while Confluence has both struck through as out of scope — the local mirror is stale. And Confluence puts PDP stories "ready for development" on 24 Aug, with the design still marked *"Done, minor update required"*. Four agents still running — design spec, code state, review threads, and convention fit. I'll hold the scope questions until those land, since the answer to "who owns the breadcrumb" partly depends on how much of it is actually built.
