## What was built

A PDP static-info panel: 3 new components + a new page + a theme recipe + 10 Playwright scenarios. 24 commits, ~9 of which are reactive CodeRabbit churn. The last two commits are the author *starting* to migrate styling into theme recipes — done for one component, abandoned for the rest. **The branch is mid-refactor.**

| Component | Data-fetching | Story | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:17` — grid, grey gallery placeholder, breadcrumb toolbar | yes (correct — it's a page) | yes (but see below) | **none** |
| `components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:26` — h1/price/description/model/style-code | no | yes + `play` | none |
| `components/breadcrumb/index.tsx:47` — nav/ol/li, Home + categories + terminal crumb | no | yes + `play` | none |
| `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:39` — 3-variant padded wrapper | no | yes | none |

## Verification (actual output)

- **`npx tsc --noEmit` — PASS**, no diagnostics.
- **`npm run lint` — FAIL.** 22 errors. **5 belong to this branch** (`breadcrumb/index.tsx:10`, `product-detail/index.tsx:16` and `:38`, `product-detail/index.stories.tsx:20` ×2 incl. `no-useless-escape`). All auto-fixable. The PR body's claim that lint passes is wrong.
- **`npx vitest run` — PASS**, 146/146 across 4 files; this branch adds 5, all for `extractModelLine`.
- **`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — the script does not exist**, despite `overrideStyling.md` mandating it pre-PR. Pre-existing repo/doc gap.
- Not run: `npm run build` — so the bundle-size impact of the new dep is **unverified** against the 180/550 kB budgets.

## Tier exposure

- **Tier 1 — `package.json:118`** gains `isomorphic-dompurify`. The PR body itself says this needs Integration approval under Hard Rule #7 and hasn't got it; commit `0068e1a` added it anyway. **16 MB installed, pulls jsdom (12 MB)**, imported at module scope on the PDP/SSR critical path. Plus `package-lock.json`.
- **Tier 2** — `routes.tsx`, `theme/components/index.ts`, `theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts` (owner: **UI Designer**, not notified).
- Hard Rule #10 (one tier per change) breached; the PR body's tier table omits both Tier 1 files and both Tier 2 theme files.
- Clean: `.github/workflows/`, `config/`, `.storybook/`, `theme/foundation/`, `ssr.js`, and every Tier 2 shared-product component.

## Two things nobody flagged in the PR

1. **`pages/product-detail/` shadows the base SFCC PDP**, and `routes.tsx:37` registers `/product/:productId` ahead of the base route. Merging this **removes add-to-bag, swatches, quantity picker, wishlist, recommendations, accordions, `<Seo>`/Helmet, and the 404 status** from the storefront PDP. May be intended scope — but it's unacknowledged.
2. **`components/breadcrumb/` shadows a shared SFCC component** used by `product-view/index.jsx:75` and `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:20` — so it **silently restyles the PLP breadcrumb** (chevron → `/`, theme config → hardcoded styles, `...rest` dropped, `categories` made required). Violates `overrideStyling.md`'s SFCC bridge-pattern rule. *(I checked and ruled out a locale-URL regression — base `categoryUrlBuilder` ignores its locale arg, so the inlined copy is behaviourally identical.)*

## Your named traps

- **Chakra scale registration — CLEAN.** Zero bare scale keys on sizing/font-size props. Every sizing prop is numeric, `%`, or a raw `var()`; typography goes through `textStyle`. `header/index.tsx:302` untouched.
- **Theme recipe collision — CLEAN.** `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is Zimm-prefixed and **registered** at `theme/components/index.ts:4,10`.
- **`var(--zimm-*)` in JSX — VIOLATED**, 8 sites: `breadcrumb:33`, `zimmPageToolbar:58`, `product-detail:52,61,62,63,69,70,71` (+ duplicated in its stories). All 15 vars *do* resolve — no dangling-var bug. The author fixed this for `PdpProductInfo` and stopped.
- **Hardcoded design values** — one: `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'` (`product-detail:14`), correctly commented as provisional, so a documented exception.
- **TypeScript-only under `overrides/` — CLEAN.**

## Also incomplete

No i18n on 4 user-facing strings (`Home`, `Style Code:`, the error message, the nav `aria-label`) despite `useIntl` already imported. `ZimmPageToolbar` padding is non-responsive (40/80px on a 375px viewport). `Pages/PDP` story **hand-duplicates the entire page JSX** rather than rendering it. `index.test.ts` sits in the page folder but tests a util. E2E fixtures only populate `au` — the other 7 storefronts fall through to a non-existent SKU and fail rather than skip. Spec filename lacks the `.p0.` priority segment so the SIT gate will never pick it up.

## Verdict

**Solid component base, unsafe integration.** `PdpProductInfo` + its theme recipe is genuinely exemplary and the a11y work is real, not claimed. But it can't merge until four *decisions* land — dependency approval, PDP-replacement scope, breadcrumb-shadow strategy, UI Designer sign-off — and two of those may restructure a meaningful slice of the code. **Don't rebase-and-continue**; resolve the decisions first, then carry the component layer forward mostly verbatim. Roughly a day of code work once unblocked.</result>

Three agents in, and the picture is now clear enough to act on. The headline finding is decisive.

## Merging PR #57 as-is would strip the PDP

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` renders exactly three things: an empty grey `<Box>` where the gallery goes ([:56](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:56)), `PdpProductInfo` ([:74](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:74)), and the breadcrumb toolbar ([:85](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:85)). The base SFCC page it replaces is 876 lines and contains `ProductView` (add-to-bag, swatches, quantity picker), `RecommendedProducts`, the information accordions, `<Helmet>`, 404 handling, and SSR cache headers.

And this isn't avoidable by fixing the route table. There are **two** independent shadowing mechanisms:

1. `overrides/app/routes.tsx:37` registers `/product/:productId` before spreading `..._routes`.
2. More fundamentally — the override mirrors the base path exactly, so `ccExtensibility` redirects base `routes.jsx:43`'s own `import('./pages/product-detail')` to the override too.

Deleting the explicit route entry changes nothing. The path mirror alone replaces the storefront PDP.

I don't think this is malice or carelessness — SFCC-89 is genuinely scoped to static information only, and the neighbouring pieces are separate tickets (SFCC-91 swatches, SFCC-92 size/ATB, SFCC-186/187/188 gallery). The author built precisely their ticket. The problem is that this ticket's output *cannot* ship independently without regressing the page, and nothing in the PR body acknowledges that.

## Verification, actually run

`tsc --noEmit` passes. Vitest passes, 146/146. **`npm run lint` fails** — 22 errors, 5 of them this branch's, all auto-fixable; the PR body claims lint is clean. `npm run build` was never run, so the bundle impact of `isomorphic-dompurify` (16 MB installed, pulls jsdom, imported at module scope on the SSR path) is unmeasured against the 180/550 kB budgets.

## Three of my working assumptions were wrong

Worth correcting explicitly, because I'd have built on them:

- **The component registry is already on `develop`** — not an unmerged dependency, and it's fully automatic via the pre-commit hook. Components never register themselves.
- **The `ui-kits` convention is not settled.** `.claude/rules/uikit-components.md` exists only on the unmerged `f2r-implementation-workflow` branch and *contradicts* `overrideStyling.md` on develop — it forbids Chakra in ui-kit files and mandates Emotion `<Global>` + `{name}.styles.ts`, where develop mandates Chakra props + a theme recipe. The two have never coexisted. Only one ui-kit component exists today.
- **None of the PDP-adjacent overrides exist** — no `image-gallery`, `swatch-group`, `display-price`, `product-view`, `quantity-picker`. `overrideStyling.md` discusses them as though they do; it's describing an aspiration.

Also: a second branch, `SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection`, already has ~650 lines of swatch work branched off SFCC-89's *older* commit — it'll conflict in `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` when rebased.

Figma and PR-review agents are still running. Once they land I'll put the decisions to you in one go rather than piecemeal — but the shape is already clear: this needs scope and dependency rulings before any code, not a rebase-and-continue.

content.text:
Found it. This is the root cause of the P0, and it's the same object as the governance blocker.

`isomorphic-dompurify`'s **server** entry instantiates JSDOM at module-evaluation time:

```js
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
var window = new JSDOM("<!DOCTYPE html>").window;   // runs on import
var purify = DOMPurifyFactory(window);
```

`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:2` imports it at module scope, so every SSR render of `/product/*` evaluates that. Bundled into `main-server.js`, jsdom's CommonJS interop yields `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__`, and the module-scope `new JSDOM()` runs before that binding initialises — the exact `ReferenceError` in the CI log, thrown from `Module.default` (the `src_default` proxy). It explains every symptom: PDP-only, SKU-independent, homepage fine, and a *build* that succeeds because this is an evaluation-order failure, not a compile error.

So the unapproved dependency and the broken page are one problem, not two.

content.text:
Only four production dependencies exist in this repo, and `isomorphic-dompurify` is now one of them. The sanitisation need is genuinely small — two fields on one component, nothing else in `overrides/` uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.

Here's where the takeover stands. Four agents in; the Figma spec is still running but doesn't gate these decisions.

**What's genuinely good:** `PdpProductInfo` plus its `ZimmPdpProductInfo` theme recipe is the reference implementation for this codebase — correctly Zimm-prefixed, properly registered, no bare scale keys, real a11y work. Vitest and Storybook genuinely pass on the current head. The component layer is worth carrying forward almost verbatim.

**What blocks it:** the page replaces the entire storefront PDP; the one dependency added is both unapproved *and* the cause of the SSR crash; `CODEOWNERS` assigns this path to Squad B while the PR reassigns it to Squad A; and three other tickets claim overlapping scope.

Four decisions are yours, and they interact — so I'd rather get them all before touching code.

Found a governance contradiction the agents didn't surface — two files disagree on who owns this code:

- `CODEOWNERS:159` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` → **`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`**
- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` lists the same path as **Squad A** territory

CODEOWNERS is the enforcement surface, so GitHub will demand a Squad B review regardless of what the draft rules file says. Worth settling, since it determines who can actually approve this.

## Gap to spec — the functional half

| AC | State | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Product name | ✅ Built | `h1` has no `data-testid` while all four siblings do; SFCC-732 asserts a `.product-name` selector that doesn't exist |
| Price — single full price | ⚠️ Partial | Uses `product.price`, which is the *current* price, not necessarily the full one. When `currency` is absent it renders `''` — an empty element that still occupies layout rather than being omitted |
| Description | ⚠️ Partial | `shortDescription \|\| longDescription` ([:77](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:77)) is a guess — the AC doesn't say which field |
| Style code | ❌ Wrong source | Reads `product?.id` ([:79](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:79)); SFCC-26 defines it as the master style number. Latent until SFCC-91 adds variant routing, then silently wrong |
| Model copy + negative case | ❌ Wrong source | Reads `c_sizeFit`, not the `modelFit` attribute SFCC-26 created for this. And `extractModelLine`'s regex `/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i` matches only a *bare* `<li>` and only the English string — returns `undefined` on 10 of 11 locales |
| Breadcrumb | ⚠️ Partial | Leaf category omitted (the CodeRabbit loop); no `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD, which is SFCC-578's whole point; `Home` hardcoded |

**Beyond the ACs:** the SSR crash; four user-facing strings untranslated while `useIntl` is already imported; no `<Seo>`/Helmet on an SEO-critical storefront; no 404 for an unknown SKU; `var(--zimm-*)` in JSX at eight sites; toolbar padding fixed at 40/80px on a 375px viewport.

**My read on effort:** the component layer is close to done and genuinely good. The gap is roughly a day of work — but the *shape* of that day depends entirely on the page-composition decision you've held. Under "compose into base page" most of the page file is rewritten and the SSR crash likely evaporates with the dependency; under "keep replacement" the component work stands and you inherit Seo/404/parity obligations.

Still waiting on the Figma agent for the visual-fidelity half, which is the other input to that estimate. I'll hold there.

## Figma spec — with two corrections to the brief

**The tooling only half-worked.** `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` resolve against the *Figma desktop app's current selection* and ignore the `nodeId` argument entirely — they returned "You currently have nothing selected". The agent substituted read-only Plugin API traversal, which for this purpose is better (resolved variable names and modes rather than pre-rendered Tailwind). If you want those two tools working later, you'd need to select the node in Figma yourself.

**Node `3087:15747` is a PAGE, not a screen** — 67 children, 108649×41878px. And only **402** and **1440** frames exist. There is no 1023 frame; **tablet is undesigned**.

### What already matches

Seven text styles map exactly (`heading3`, `price`, `body2`, `caption`, `linkLg`, `linkSm`, `button`), four colour tokens, and the design system's spacing scale is **1:1 identical** to `spacing.ts`. That's a strong foundation — the token work from the footer build is paying off here.

The layout gaps are close but consistently off by a hair:

| Value | Figma | Code | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column gap | 179px | `--zimm-scale-4500` = 180px | ✅ rounding |
| Desktop right pad | 142px | `--zimm-scale-3500` = 140px | ⚠️ 2px |
| Mobile side pad | 30px | `--zimm-scale-800` = 32px | ⚠️ wrong token — `grid.containerPadding.base` is exactly 30px |

### The one that matters

**The info column should be 218px, not 360px.** Figma's 1440 frame is 900 gallery + 179 gap + 218 info + 142 pad. The code's `1fr 360px` yields a 760px gallery and a 360px column — the gallery loses 140px and the text column gains 142px. The author flagged `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH` as *"Provisional — pending designer sign-off"*; we now have the measured answer.

### Genuine design-side defects found (varying residuals, so not artifacts)

`body2Strong` letter-spacing is −0.12px in the repo where Figma says −0.14px — and `letterSpacings['2xs']` **already holds −0.14px**, so it's a mis-pointed token. That's `typography.ts`, Tier 1, so it needs the UI Designer regardless. Also `#000000` hardcoded on two labels where everything else uses `text/default`, and a layer named "Size & Fit" that renders "Details & Care".

**Out of scope but worth logging:** the mobile wishlist target is 20×20, below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24×24 minimum — that's SFCC-434's problem, but someone should know now rather than at audit.

**A trap not to fall into:** the DS typography collection is mode-switched (`body-2` = 14px desktop / 12px mobile), but *neither frame actually switches modes* — both resolve identically. Don't build a responsive font-size step on the strength of the mode existing.

**Needs a designer decision, invented nothing:** six off-scale spacing values (6/15/22/28/43/44) absent from both the repo and the DS scale, the undesigned tablet range, and 9px/13px chevrons.

One useful side-effect: the button measures 50/5/24 on a CSS-comparable instance at both breakpoints, which **confirms `button.ts`'s provisional constants and contradicts `actionSizes` (52/32)** — that's a standing open item in `overrideStyling.md` now answerable.

---

## Where this leaves the estimate

Roughly a day, and the split is clearer now:

**Decision-independent — I could start on these now:** the 5 lint errors (all auto-fixable), the four untranslated strings, the missing `data-testid` on the `h1`, the eight `var(--zimm-*)` sites moving from JSX into the recipe, mobile padding 32→30, and the column width 360→218.

**Blocked on your four held decisions:** page composition, the sanitiser/SSR crash, `modelFit` vs `c_sizeFit`, breadcrumb ownership, and anything touching `typography.ts`.

Want me to start on the decision-independent set while you settle the rest, or hold everything until the scope questions land?

# SFCC-89 / PR #57 — Consolidated Findings

Investigation date: 2026-08-22. Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`.
Branch: `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`.

This is the authoritative summary. Five deeper reports sit alongside it in the same folder:
`req-jira.md`, `req-figma.md`, `code-state.md`, `pr57-review.md`, `conventions.md`, plus
`pr57-body.md` (the PR description verbatim).

---

## 0. Situation

We are **taking over an in-flight PR authored by someone else**. PR #57
"feat(pdp): SFCC-89 — PDP UI static product information", author **JhoanDelaCruz**,
opened 2026-08-18, last pushed 2026-08-21. 24 commits, +1702/−99 across 30 files.
Base `develop`. State OPEN / `CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `MERGEABLE` / `BLOCKED`.
0 commits behind develop.

The four scope decisions (page composition, ticket ownership, sanitiser, PR strategy)
have been **deliberately deferred by the FED Lead**. Work continues on the existing
branch for now. No code has been changed. No commits. No pushes.

---

## 1. What SFCC-89 asks for

Story, High, 5 points, Sprint 3 (10–24 Aug), status **Code Review**, assignee Jhoan
Rose Dela Cruz, reporter Jasmijn Tsang, due 17 Aug (overdue). Parent epic **SFCC-5
(PDP)** — a Level 2 *page* epic.

**The acceptance criteria are in a custom field (`customfield_10231`), not the
description** — easy to miss entirely. Six Given/When/Then items:

1. Product name
2. Price — single full price, in storefront currency
3. Description
4. Style code
5. Model copy ("Model is…"), including the negative case (no empty placeholder)
6. Breadcrumb beneath the product images: `HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]`,
   nodes navigate to category

Two further styling ACs live in standalone Tasks **SFCC-732 / SFCC-733** (both To Do),
citing Figma node `5804-170721`. They assert `.product-name` / `.product-price` CSS
selectors that **the component does not expose** — values match, selectors do not, so
they fail at QA as written.

**Explicitly out of scope**, with owning tickets: badges (SFCC-132/225), was/now pricing
(SFCC-194), wishlist (SFCC-434), colour swatches (SFCC-91), size + add-to-bag (SFCC-92),
Find in Boutique (SFCC-297), image gallery (SFCC-186/187/188), accordions
(SFCC-195/102/267/266).

---

## 2. Findings ranked by severity

### P0-A — Merging this removes the storefront PDP

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (95 lines) replaces the base SFCC PDP
(876 lines). It renders exactly three things: an empty grey `<Box>` placeholder for the
gallery (`:56`), `<PdpProductInfo>` (`:74`), and the breadcrumb toolbar (`:85`).

Everything else in the base page disappears: `ProductView` (add-to-bag, swatches,
quantity picker), `RecommendedProducts`, `InformationAccordion`, `<Helmet>`/`<Seo>`,
`HTTPNotFound` 404 handling, SSR cache headers, `<Island>` hydration, and the full
`useProduct` expand list.

**Two independent shadowing mechanisms, so deleting the route entry does not fix it:**
1. `overrides/app/routes.tsx:37` registers `/product/:productId` before `..._routes`.
2. The override mirrors the base path exactly, so `ccExtensibility` redirects base
   `routes.jsx:43`'s own `import('./pages/product-detail')` to the override too.

Verified directly, not inferred. Nothing in the PR body acknowledges this.

### P0-B — The PDP throws on every SSR request, and the cause is the unapproved dependency

CI artifact shows, for every `/product/*` request, valid and invalid SKU alike:

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access '__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__' before initialization
    at Module.default (build/main-server.js:71360:42)
```

**Root cause established by direct inspection.** `isomorphic-dompurify`'s node entry
(`dist/index.mjs`) instantiates JSDOM at module-evaluation time:

```js
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
var window = new JSDOM("<!DOCTYPE html>").window;   // runs on import
var purify = DOMPurifyFactory(window);
```

`overrides/app/components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:2` imports it at module scope. Bundled
into `main-server.js`, jsdom's CommonJS interop produces `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__`, and
the module-scope `new JSDOM()` executes before that binding initialises. Explains every
symptom: PDP-only, SKU-independent, homepage unaffected, and a *build* that succeeds
because this is an evaluation-order failure, not a compile error.

Consequence: Playwright went **0-for-7** on PDP scenarios (6 retries exhausted, 2 skipped)
then hit the 15-minute job timeout; `mobile-chrome` never ran; no HTML report produced.
**The PR body attributes these failures to missing sandbox products. That is not what is
happening.**

I ruled out a circular import in our own code: a value-import cycle scan across
`overrides/app` (110 modules reachable from the PDP entry, resolving base-package imports
through the override redirect) found **no cycles**. The only two hits were override files
importing their own base path, which is the documented PWA Kit self-reference pattern.

### P0-C — Tier 1 dependency added without approval

`package.json` gains `isomorphic-dompurify@^3.19.0` as a **production** dependency
(commit `0068e1a`). `package.json` is Tier 1 frozen; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 forbids adding
packages without Integration team approval. **The PR body itself states the approval is
needed and has not been obtained** — then the dependency was added anyway.

Context: the repo has only **four** production dependencies total. The lockfile shows the
install flipped a chain of jsdom-related packages (`@asamuzakjp/*` and others) from
`dev: true` into the production tree. 16 MB installed, jsdom ~12 MB.

Scope of the actual need is tiny: **two** `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sites, both in
`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` (`:43` description, `:54` model info). Nothing else in
`overrides/` uses it.

**Measured, not assumed:** I ran `npm run build`. It succeeds. Bundle budgets **pass** —
`main.js` 103.46 KB gzip (limit 180 KB), `vendor.js` 524.74 KB gzip (limit 550 KB).
Note vendor is at **95.4% of budget** with ~25 KB headroom. No circular-dependency warning
was emitted, but webpack does not emit those by default.

### P1 — Multi-tier change (Hard Rule #10)

- **Tier 1:** `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
- **Tier 2:** `routes.tsx`, `theme/components/index.ts`, `theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts`
  (owner: **UI Designer** — not notified)
- Clean: `.github/workflows/`, `config/`, `.storybook/`, `theme/foundation/`, `ssr.js`,
  and every Tier 2 shared-product component.

The PR body's changed-files table lists **15 files and omits every Tier 1 file**. The real
diff is 30 files.

### P1 — Ownership contradiction between two governance files

- `CODEOWNERS:159` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` → **`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`**
- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` lists the same path as **Squad A** territory

CODEOWNERS is the enforcement surface, so GitHub will require a Squad B review regardless.
This PR also reclassifies ProductDetail to Squad A in the generated registry. Unresolved.

### P1 — Breadcrumb silently restyles the PLP

`overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/` shadows a **shared SFCC component** consumed by
`product-view/index.jsx:75` and `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:20`. Effects:
chevron separator → `/`, theme config → hardcoded styles, `...rest` dropped, `categories`
made required. Violates the SFCC bridge-pattern rule in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(shared components must keep a faithful, undecorated default export; brand styling goes
behind a named export or a theme recipe).

*Ruled out:* a suspected locale-URL regression — base `categoryUrlBuilder` ignores its
locale argument, so the inlined copy is behaviourally identical.

### P1 — No human has reviewed this PR

All **8 reviews and all 22 inline threads are `coderabbitai[bot]`**. The
`CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision is entirely the bot's. Five reviewer teams were requested —
PWA Squad A, PWA Squad B, PWA QA, Tier-1 Approvers, Tier-2 Approvers — **none responded**.
The only human comments are the author's own note about a BrowserStack secret and
`marcelannavarro` typing `@coderabbitai full-review`.

---

## 3. Acceptance-criteria conformance

| AC | State | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Product name | Built | `h1` has no `data-testid` while all four siblings do; SFCC-732 asserts `.product-name`, which does not exist |
| Price — single full price | Partial | Uses `product.price` (current price, not necessarily full). When `currency` is absent, renders `''` — an empty element that still occupies layout instead of being omitted |
| Description | Partial | `shortDescription \|\| longDescription` (`page:77`) is a guess; the AC does not say which field |
| Style code | **Wrong source** | Reads `product?.id` (`page:79`). SFCC-26 defines style code as the **master** ID / `styleNumber`. Latent until SFCC-91 adds colour-variant routing, then silently wrong |
| Model copy + negative case | **Wrong source** | Reads `c_sizeFit`, not the `modelFit` attribute SFCC-26 created specifically for this line. Jasmijn's comments confirm `modelFit` was deliberate. `sizeFit` belongs to the Size & Fit tab (SFCC-102, out of scope) |
| Breadcrumb | Partial | Leaf category omitted; no `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD (the whole point of SFCC-578); `Home` hardcoded |

`extractModelLine` (`overrides/app/utils/productData.ts`) is:

```ts
const match = html.match(/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i);
```

Two defects: matches only a **bare** `<li>` (any attribute breaks it), and matches only the
**English** string. Returns `undefined` on 10 of 11 locales.

---

## 4. Figma design spec

Design: `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states), node `3087:15747`.
**Never cross-compare with `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (the design system file).**

**Two corrections to the original brief:**
- `3087:15747` is a **PAGE**, not a screen — 67 children, 108649×41878 px.
- Only **402** and **1440** frames exist. **No 1023 frame. Tablet is undesigned.**
  Repo breakpoints are `md 768` / `xl 1280`; **no `860` token exists anywhere in the theme.**

**Tooling limits hit:** `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` resolve against the
Figma **desktop app's current selection** and ignore the `nodeId` argument — both returned
"You currently have nothing selected". Substituted read-only Plugin API traversal, which
gives resolved variable names/collections/modes rather than pre-rendered Tailwind.
`get_metadata` on the target fails deterministically (subtree >315 KB vs the SSE cap). A
non-ASCII character in some layer names breaks SSE encoding outright.

**Measurement rules applied.** TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, not comparable to a CSS
line box. FRAMES/INSTANCES report real boxes and are comparable. A **third case** was
found that the brief did not cover: **a FRAME that hugs a TEXT child inherits the
cap-height artifact** — accordion rows report `218x9`, which is text cap-height, not row
height (real pitch ≈ 25.5 px). Uniform residual = artifact; varying residual = defect.

### Matches
Seven text styles map exactly (`heading3`, `price`, `body2`, `caption`, `linkLg`,
`linkSm`, `button`), four colour tokens, spacing 2/4/8/16/24/30/80. The DS spacing scale
is **1:1 identical** to `spacing.ts`.

### Layout — measured vs code

| Value | Figma | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column gap | 179px | `--zimm-scale-4500` = **180px** | rounding, fine |
| Desktop right pad | 142px | `--zimm-scale-3500` = **140px** | 2px off |
| Mobile side pad | 30px (x=30) | `--zimm-scale-800` = **32px** | wrong token — `grid.containerPadding.base` is exactly `30px` |
| **Info column width** | **218px** | **`PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'`** | **142px off** |

Desktop composition: 900 gallery + 179 gap + 218 info + 142 pad = 1439 ≈ 1440.
The code's `1fr 360px` yields a **760px gallery and a 360px info column** — gallery loses
140px, text column gains 142px. The author annotated the constant *"Provisional — no
matching zimm token; pending designer sign-off"*, so this was a known guess; we now have
the measured answer.

Mobile info column 342px at x=30 — matches `grid.containerPadding.base` exactly.
**All layout gaps are identical across breakpoints** (28/44/22/16/8/15/2); only width and
three icon sizes change.

### Design-side defects (all varying residuals — matching values matched at exactly 0px)
- `body2Strong` letter-spacing is **−0.12px** in the repo, **−0.14px** in Figma. The
  correct token **already exists**: `letterSpacings['2xs'] = '-0.00875rem' // -0.14px`
  (`typography.ts:27`). It is a mis-pointed token, not a missing one. **`typography.ts` is
  Tier 1** — UI Designer required.
- `#000000` hardcoded on two labels where everything else uses `text/default`.
- Product name uses a different style on mobile than desktop.
- **Mobile wishlist target is 20×20 — below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24×24 minimum.** (SFCC-434's
  ticket, but it should be known now, not at audit.)
- A layer named `Size & Fit` renders `Details & Care`.

### Resolves a standing repo open item
The button measures **50 / 5 / 24** on a CSS-comparable INSTANCE at **both** breakpoints —
confirming `button.ts`'s "provisional" `BTN_HEIGHT_LG` / `BTN_PADDING_Y` constants and
**contradicting `actionSizes` (52/32)**. `overrideStyling.md` lists this as an open gap; it
is now answerable.

### Trap — do not implement
The DS Typography collection is mode-switched (`body-2` = 14px desktop / 12px mobile), **but
neither frame switches modes** — both resolve to the same mode id, so rendered sizes are
identical. Do **not** build a responsive font-size step on the strength of the mode existing.

### Token gaps needing a designer decision (nothing invented)
Six off-scale spacing values — **6 / 15 / 22 / 28 / 43 / 44** — absent from the repo *and*
from the DS's own scale. Plus the undesigned tablet range and the 9px/13px chevrons.

---

## 5. Verification actually run (not assumed)

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | **PASS**, no diagnostics |
| `npm run lint` | **FAIL** — 22 errors, **5 belong to this branch** (`breadcrumb/index.tsx:10`, `product-detail/index.tsx:16` and `:38`, `product-detail/index.stories.tsx:20` ×2 incl. `no-useless-escape`). All auto-fixable. **The PR body claims lint passes. It does not.** |
| `npx vitest run` | **PASS** — 146/146 across 4 files; this branch adds 5, all for `extractModelLine` |
| `npm run build` | **PASS** |
| `npm run test:max-file-size` | **PASS** — main 103.46 KB / 180 KB; vendor 524.74 KB / 550 KB (95.4% of budget) |
| `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | **Script does not exist**, despite `overrideStyling.md` mandating it pre-PR. Pre-existing repo/doc gap |

**CI reality on the current head:** Vitest (146/146) and Storybook (27/27) genuinely
executed and passed. **But** two earlier runs on 2026-08-20 (`cf17c3d`, `d904c63`) are
recorded **green with every test job `skipped`** — the `detect-changes`
`since_last_remote_commit: true` trap. A skipped required check looks green and proves
nothing. **E2E is not a required check** — only `Storybook`, `Unit tests (Vitest)` and
`🔴 Branch Target Check` gate `develop`, so the entire red E2E suite does not block merge.
`🔴 Tier 1 — Frozen Files Check` reports "pass" but **did** flag `package.json` +
`package-lock.json` — that step only echoes a warning by design.

**Gated nowhere:** `eslint`, `prettier`, `tsc --noEmit`. Zero matches across all 15
workflows and none of the three husky hooks. **Storybook a11y IS gated** —
`.storybook/preview.tsx:34-36` sets `a11y.test: 'error'`, `@storybook/test-runner` reads it
directly, no `test-runner.js` exists or is needed, `qa.yml:262` invokes the binary.

**Side effect I caused and reverted:** `npm run build` runs `build-translations` first,
which regenerated 5 translation files (adding `header.button.assistive_msg.search`, a base
SFCC string — so the committed translations were already mildly stale). I reverted all
five; working tree is clean. Those files are Tier 2 (Integration/SI Partner).

---

## 6. Convention and structure findings

### Three premises that turned out wrong
1. **The component registry is NOT an unmerged dependency.** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`,
   `.claude/registry/*.md`, `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` are all on `develop`. It is
   fully automatic — components never register themselves; `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:49-62`
   regenerates and stages on every commit.
2. **The `ui-kits` convention is NOT settled.** `.claude/rules/uikit-components.md` exists
   only on the unmerged `origin/feature/f2r-implementation-workflow` branch and **directly
   contradicts `overrideStyling.md` on `develop`**: it *forbids* Chakra inside ui-kit files
   and mandates per-component `{name}.styles.ts` + Emotion `<Global>`, where
   `overrideStyling.md` mandates Chakra props + a theme recipe. The two never coexist on
   any branch. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/` contains exactly **one** component
   (`atoms/zimmPageToolbar/`). No `molecules/`, no `organisms/`. Needs a ruling.
3. **None of the PDP-adjacent SFCC overrides exist** — `image-gallery`, `swatch-group`,
   `display-price`, `product-tile`, `product-item`, `recommended-products`, `product-view`,
   `quantity-picker`: zero files on HEAD *and* on `develop`. `overrideStyling.md` discusses
   several at length as if they exist; it is describing an aspiration.

### Three override intercept traps
- **(a) Storybook/Vitest resolver gap — real, confirmed, not currently triggered.**
  `.storybook/main.js:25` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` straight to `node_modules`;
  `vitest.config.ts` never mentions it. So a base-path import of an already-overridden
  component renders/tests the **unstyled base** in Storybook and Vitest while working in the
  app. The only current base-path/override collision is `icons`, which is deliberate. **It
  goes live the moment PDP overrides `swatch-group` / `image-gallery` / `display-price` /
  `quantity-picker`** — all of which `product-view` imports by base path.
- **(b) `shared/ui` barrel — confirmed with numbers.** 103 relative re-exports; **212** base
  files import the barrel, **0** import a deep path. Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
  intercepts nothing. PDP does not depend on this and should not start.
- **(c) Conditional module swap — no PDP equivalent.** The `_app` checkout swap
  (`_app/index.jsx:216,484`) never matches `/product/:productId`.

### Data layer
`useProduct` / `useCategory` are called only in the page (`:21-31`); components are pure —
the container/presentational rule is obeyed. Type resolves to
`ShopperProductsModelTypes.Product`, everything optional except `id`, with an

Investigation date: 2026-08-22. Repo: `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa`.
Branch: `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`.

This is the authoritative summary. Five deeper reports sit alongside it in the same folder:
`req-jira.md`, `req-figma.md`, `code-state.md`, `pr57-review.md`, `conventions.md`, plus
`pr57-body.md` (the PR description verbatim).

---

## 0. Situation

We are **taking over an in-flight PR authored by someone else**. PR #57
"feat(pdp): SFCC-89 — PDP UI static product information", author **JhoanDelaCruz**,
opened 2026-08-18, last pushed 2026-08-21. 24 commits, +1702/−99 across 30 files.
Base `develop`. State OPEN / `CHANGES_REQUESTED` / `MERGEABLE` / `BLOCKED`.
0 commits behind develop.

The four scope decisions (page composition, ticket ownership, sanitiser, PR strategy)
have been **deliberately deferred by the FED Lead**. Work continues on the existing
branch for now. No code has been changed. No commits. No pushes.

---

## 1. What SFCC-89 asks for

Story, High, 5 points, Sprint 3 (10–24 Aug), status **Code Review**, assignee Jhoan
Rose Dela Cruz, reporter Jasmijn Tsang, due 17 Aug (overdue). Parent epic **SFCC-5
(PDP)** — a Level 2 *page* epic.

**The acceptance criteria are in a custom field (`customfield_10231`), not the
description** — easy to miss entirely. Six Given/When/Then items:

1. Product name
2. Price — single full price, in storefront currency
3. Description
4. Style code
5. Model copy ("Model is…"), including the negative case (no empty placeholder)
6. Breadcrumb beneath the product images: `HOME / NEW / DRESSES / [PRODUCT NAME]`,
   nodes navigate to category

Two further styling ACs live in standalone Tasks **SFCC-732 / SFCC-733** (both To Do),
citing Figma node `5804-170721`. They assert `.product-name` / `.product-price` CSS
selectors that **the component does not expose** — values match, selectors do not, so
they fail at QA as written.

**Explicitly out of scope**, with owning tickets: badges (SFCC-132/225), was/now pricing
(SFCC-194), wishlist (SFCC-434), colour swatches (SFCC-91), size + add-to-bag (SFCC-92),
Find in Boutique (SFCC-297), image gallery (SFCC-186/187/188), accordions
(SFCC-195/102/267/266).

---

## 2. Findings ranked by severity

### P0-A — Merging this removes the storefront PDP

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (95 lines) replaces the base SFCC PDP
(876 lines). It renders exactly three things: an empty grey `<Box>` placeholder for the
gallery (`:56`), `<PdpProductInfo>` (`:74`), and the breadcrumb toolbar (`:85`).

Everything else in the base page disappears: `ProductView` (add-to-bag, swatches,
quantity picker), `RecommendedProducts`, `InformationAccordion`, `<Helmet>`/`<Seo>`,
`HTTPNotFound` 404 handling, SSR cache headers, `<Island>` hydration, and the full
`useProduct` expand list.

**Two independent shadowing mechanisms, so deleting the route entry does not fix it:**
1. `overrides/app/routes.tsx:37` registers `/product/:productId` before `..._routes`.
2. The override mirrors the base path exactly, so `ccExtensibility` redirects base
   `routes.jsx:43`'s own `import('./pages/product-detail')` to the override too.

Verified directly, not inferred. Nothing in the PR body acknowledges this.

### P0-B — The PDP throws on every SSR request, and the cause is the unapproved dependency

CI artifact shows, for every `/product/*` request, valid and invalid SKU alike:

```
ReferenceError: Cannot access '__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__' before initialization
    at Module.default (build/main-server.js:71360:42)
```

**Root cause established by direct inspection.** `isomorphic-dompurify`'s node entry
(`dist/index.mjs`) instantiates JSDOM at module-evaluation time:

```js
import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";
var window = new JSDOM("<!DOCTYPE html>").window;   // runs on import
var purify = DOMPurifyFactory(window);
```

`overrides/app/components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:2` imports it at module scope. Bundled
into `main-server.js`, jsdom's CommonJS interop produces `__WEBPACK_DEFAULT_EXPORT__`, and
the module-scope `new JSDOM()` executes before that binding initialises. Explains every
symptom: PDP-only, SKU-independent, homepage unaffected, and a *build* that succeeds
because this is an evaluation-order failure, not a compile error.

Consequence: Playwright went **0-for-7** on PDP scenarios (6 retries exhausted, 2 skipped)
then hit the 15-minute job timeout; `mobile-chrome` never ran; no HTML report produced.
**The PR body attributes these failures to missing sandbox products. That is not what is
happening.**

I ruled out a circular import in our own code: a value-import cycle scan across
`overrides/app` (110 modules reachable from the PDP entry, resolving base-package imports
through the override redirect) found **no cycles**. The only two hits were override files
importing their own base path, which is the documented PWA Kit self-reference pattern.

### P0-C — Tier 1 dependency added without approval

`package.json` gains `isomorphic-dompurify@^3.19.0` as a **production** dependency
(commit `0068e1a`). `package.json` is Tier 1 frozen; AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7 forbids adding
packages without Integration team approval. **The PR body itself states the approval is
needed and has not been obtained** — then the dependency was added anyway.

Context: the repo has only **four** production dependencies total. The lockfile shows the
install flipped a chain of jsdom-related packages (`@asamuzakjp/*` and others) from
`dev: true` into the production tree. 16 MB installed, jsdom ~12 MB.

Scope of the actual need is tiny: **two** `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` sites, both in
`pdpProductInfo/index.tsx` (`:43` description, `:54` model info). Nothing else in
`overrides/` uses it.

**Measured, not assumed:** I ran `npm run build`. It succeeds. Bundle budgets **pass** —
`main.js` 103.46 KB gzip (limit 180 KB), `vendor.js` 524.74 KB gzip (limit 550 KB).
Note vendor is at **95.4% of budget** with ~25 KB headroom. No circular-dependency warning
was emitted, but webpack does not emit those by default.

### P1 — Multi-tier change (Hard Rule #10)

- **Tier 1:** `package.json`, `package-lock.json`
- **Tier 2:** `routes.tsx`, `theme/components/index.ts`, `theme/components/pdpProductInfo.ts`
  (owner: **UI Designer** — not notified)
- Clean: `.github/workflows/`, `config/`, `.storybook/`, `theme/foundation/`, `ssr.js`,
  and every Tier 2 shared-product component.

The PR body's changed-files table lists **15 files and omits every Tier 1 file**. The real
diff is 30 files.

### P1 — Ownership contradiction between two governance files

- `CODEOWNERS:159` → `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` → **`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b`**
- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` lists the same path as **Squad A** territory

CODEOWNERS is the enforcement surface, so GitHub will require a Squad B review regardless.
This PR also reclassifies ProductDetail to Squad A in the generated registry. Unresolved.

### P1 — Breadcrumb silently restyles the PLP

`overrides/app/components/breadcrumb/` shadows a **shared SFCC component** consumed by
`product-view/index.jsx:75` and `product-list/partials/page-header.jsx:20`. Effects:
chevron separator → `/`, theme config → hardcoded styles, `...rest` dropped, `categories`
made required. Violates the SFCC bridge-pattern rule in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(shared components must keep a faithful, undecorated default export; brand styling goes
behind a named export or a theme recipe).

*Ruled out:* a suspected locale-URL regression — base `categoryUrlBuilder` ignores its
locale argument, so the inlined copy is behaviourally identical.

### P1 — No human has reviewed this PR

All **8 reviews and all 22 inline threads are `coderabbitai[bot]`**. The
`CHANGES_REQUESTED` decision is entirely the bot's. Five reviewer teams were requested —
PWA Squad A, PWA Squad B, PWA QA, Tier-1 Approvers, Tier-2 Approvers — **none responded**.
The only human comments are the author's own note about a BrowserStack secret and
`marcelannavarro` typing `@coderabbitai full-review`.

## 3. Acceptance-criteria conformance

| AC | State | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Product name | Built | `h1` has no `data-testid` while all four siblings do; SFCC-732 asserts `.product-name`, which does not exist |
| Price — single full price | Partial | Uses `product.price` (current price, not necessarily full). When `currency` is absent, renders `''` — an empty element that still occupies layout instead of being omitted |
| Description | Partial | `shortDescription \|\| longDescription` (`page:77`) is a guess; the AC does not say which field |
| Style code | **Wrong source** | Reads `product?.id` (`page:79`). SFCC-26 defines style code as the **master** ID / `styleNumber`. Latent until SFCC-91 adds colour-variant routing, then silently wrong |
| Model copy + negative case | **Wrong source** | Reads `c_sizeFit`, not the `modelFit` attribute SFCC-26 created specifically for this line. Jasmijn's comments confirm `modelFit` was deliberate. `sizeFit` belongs to the Size & Fit tab (SFCC-102, out of scope) |

`extractModelLine` (`overrides/app/utils/productData.ts`) is:

```ts
const match = html.match(/<li>\s*(Model is[^<]*?)\s*<\/li>/i);
```

Two defects: matches only a **bare** `<li>` (any attribute breaks it), and matches only the
**English** string. Returns `undefined` on 10 of 11 locales.

---

## 4. Figma design spec

Design: `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states), node `3087:15747`.
**Never cross-compare with `wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (the design system file).**

**Two corrections to the original brief:**
- `3087:15747` is a **PAGE**, not a screen — 67 children, 108649×41878 px.
- Only **402** and **1440** frames exist. **No 1023 frame. Tablet is undesigned.**
  Repo breakpoints are `md 768` / `xl 1280`; **no `860` token exists anywhere in the theme.**

**Tooling limits hit:** `get_variable_defs` and `get_design_context` resolve against the
Figma **desktop app's current selection** and ignore the `nodeId` argument — both returned

gives resolved variable names/collections/modes rather than pre-rendered Tailwind.
`get_metadata` on the target fails deterministically (subtree >315 KB vs the SSE cap). A
non-ASCII character in some layer names breaks SSE encoding outright.

**Measurement rules applied.** TEXT nodes report a cap-height box, not comparable to a CSS
line box. FRAMES/INSTANCES report real boxes and are comparable. A **third case** was
found that the brief did not cover: **a FRAME that hugs a TEXT child inherits the
cap-height artifact** — accordion rows report `218x9`, which is text cap-height, not row
height (real pitch ≈ 25.5 px). Uniform residual = artifact; varying residual = defect.

### Matches
Seven text styles map exactly (`heading3`, `price`, `body2`, `caption`, `linkLg`,
`linkSm`, `button`), four colour tokens, spacing 2/4/8/16/24/30/80. The DS spacing scale
is **1:1 identical** to `spacing.ts`.

### Layout — measured vs code

| Value | Figma | Code | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Column gap | 179px | `--zimm-scale-4500` = **180px** | rounding, fine |
| Desktop right pad | 142px | `--zimm-scale-3500` = **140px** | 2px off |
| Mobile side pad | 30px (x=30) | `--zimm-scale-800` = **32px** | wrong token — `grid.containerPadding.base` is exactly `30px` |
| **Info column width** | **218px** | **`PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'`** | **142px off** |

Desktop composition: 900 gallery + 179 gap + 218 info + 142 pad = 1439 ≈ 1440.
The code's `1fr 360px` yields a **760px gallery and a 360px info column** — gallery loses
140px, text column gains 142px. The author annotated the constant *"Provisional — no
matching zimm token; pending designer sign-off"*, so this was a known guess; we now have
the measured answer.

Mobile info column 342px at x=30 — matches `grid.containerPadding.base` exactly.
**All layout gaps are identical across breakpoints** (28/44/22/16/8/15/2); only width and
three icon sizes change.

### Design-side defects (all varying residuals — matching values matched at exactly 0px)
- `body2Strong` letter-spacing is **−0.12px** in the repo, **−0.14px** in Figma. The
  correct token **already exists**: `letterSpacings['2xs'] = '-0.00875rem' // -0.14px`
  (`typography.ts:27`). It is a mis-pointed token, not a missing one. **`typography.ts` is
  Tier 1** — UI Designer required.
- `#000000` hardcoded on two labels where everything else uses `text/default`.
- Product name uses a different style on mobile than desktop.
- **Mobile wishlist target is 20×20 — below the WCAG 2.2 AA 24×24 minimum.** (SFCC-434's
  ticket, but it should be known now, not at audit.)
- A layer named `Size & Fit` renders `Details & Care`.

### Resolves a standing repo open item
The button measures **50 / 5 / 24** on a CSS-comparable INSTANCE at **both** breakpoints —
confirming `button.ts`'s "provisional" `BTN_HEIGHT_LG` / `BTN_PADDING_Y` constants and
**contradicting `actionSizes` (52/32)**. `overrideStyling.md` lists this as an open gap; it
is now answerable.

### Trap — do not implement
The DS Typography collection is mode-switched (`body-2` = 14px desktop / 12px mobile), **but
neither frame switches modes** — both resolve to the same mode id, so rendered sizes are
identical. Do **not** build a responsive font-size step on the strength of the mode existing.

### Token gaps needing a designer decision (nothing invented)
Six off-scale spacing values — **6 / 15 / 22 / 28 / 43 / 44** — absent from the repo *and*
from the DS's own scale. Plus the undesigned tablet range and the 9px/13px chevrons.

## 5. Verification actually run (not assumed)

## 6. Convention and structure findings

### Three premises that turned out wrong
1. **The component registry is NOT an unmerged dependency.** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`,

2. **The `ui-kits` convention is NOT settled.** `.claude/rules/uikit-components.md` exists

   contradicts `overrideStyling.md` on `develop`**: it *forbids* Chakra inside ui-kit files

  goes live the moment PDP overrides `swatch-group` / `image-gallery` / `display-price` /
  `quantity-picker`** — all of which `product-view` imports by base path.
- **(b) `shared/ui` barrel — confirmed with numbers.** 103 relative re-exports; **212** base
  files import the barrel, **0** import a deep path. Overriding `shared/ui/<Name>` therefore
  intercepts nothing. PDP does not depend on this and should not start.
- **(c) Conditional module swap — no PDP equivalent.** The `_app` checkout swap
  (`_app/index.jsx:216,484`) never matches `/product/:productId`.

### Data layer
`useProduct` / `useCategory` are called only in the page (`:21-31`); components are pure —
the container/presentational rule is obeyed. Type resolves to
`ShopperProductsModelTypes.Product`, everything optional except `id`, with an
`& {[key:string]: any}` tail. The repo deliberately does not lean on that tail:
`ProductWithSizeFit` derives from `ReturnType<typeof useProduct>` and narrows `c_sizeFit`
to `string`. Copy that pattern for each new `c_*` field.

### Reuse item that would otherwise be missed
`overrides/app/utils/sfccImage.ts`'s `proxyImageUrl()` rewrites SFCC image URLs through the
PWA Kit proxy, because direct Demandware-host access is **Cloudflare-WAF-blocked outside the
CC network**. Any gallery work rendering `imageGroups[].images[].link` without it will 403
for real shoppers.

### Coordination
`origin/feature/SFCC-91_pdp-ui-colour-swatches-variation-selection` branches off SFCC-89 at
the **older** commit `d904c63` and already contains ~650 lines of swatch component + tests +
stories plus an 883-line spec. It is missing SFCC-89's last two commits, so rebasing will
conflict in `pdpProductInfo/index.tsx`. **Adopt it, do not rewrite it.**

---

## 7. Component-by-component

| Component | Data-fetching | Story | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pages/product-detail/index.tsx:17` — grid, grey gallery placeholder, breadcrumb toolbar | yes (correct — it is a page) | yes (but hand-duplicates the entire page JSX rather than rendering it) | none |
| `components/pdpProductInfo/index.tsx:26` — h1 / price / description / model / style code | no | yes + `play` | none |
| `components/breadcrumb/index.tsx:47` — nav/ol/li, Home + categories + terminal crumb | no | yes + `play` | none |
| `components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmPageToolbar/index.tsx:39` — 3-variant padded wrapper | no | yes | none |

24 commits, ~9 of them reactive CodeRabbit churn. **The last two commits are the author
starting to migrate styling into theme recipes — done for `PdpProductInfo`, abandoned for
the rest. The branch is mid-refactor.**

### Named traps — results
- **Chakra scale registration — CLEAN.** Zero bare scale keys on sizing/font-size props.
  Every sizing prop is numeric, `%`, or a raw `var()`; typography goes through `textStyle`.
  The known live bug at `header/index.tsx:302` is untouched.
- **Theme recipe collision — CLEAN.** `ZimmPdpProductInfo` is Zimm-prefixed and **registered**
  at `theme/components/index.ts:4,10`.
- **`var(--zimm-*)` in JSX — VIOLATED at 8 sites:** `breadcrumb:33`, `zimmPageToolbar:58`,
  `product-detail:52,61,62,63,69,70,71` (plus duplicates in its stories). All 15 vars *do*
  resolve — no dangling-var bug. The author fixed this for `PdpProductInfo` and stopped.
- **Hardcoded design values — one:** `PDP_OPTIONS_COLUMN_WIDTH = '360px'`
  (`product-detail:14`), correctly commented as provisional — a documented exception.
- **TypeScript-only under `overrides/` — CLEAN.**

### Incomplete / stubbed
- **No i18n on four user-facing strings** — `Home`, `Style Code:` (`pdpProductInfo:59`), the
  error message (`product-detail:66`), and the nav `aria-label` — despite `useIntl` already
  being imported.
- `ZimmPageToolbar` padding is non-responsive (40/80px on a 375px viewport).
- `index.test.ts` sits in the page folder but tests a util.
- E2E fixtures only populate `au`; the other 7 storefronts fall through to a non-existent
  SKU and **fail rather than skip**.
- Spec filename lacks the `.p0.` priority segment, so the SIT gate will never pick it up.
- `qa.yml` has **no `e2e_pdp` allow-list group**, so every PDP change falls back to the full
  Playwright suite.

---

## 8. Unresolved bot findings (8 of 22)

CodeRabbit's last pass ran against `d526ad1`, which **is** the head — so **no unresolved
finding is moot**; all 8 target current code.

- **Still valid:** U1 `products.js:29` cross-site SKU fallback · U5 `productData.ts:7` regex
  matches only bare `<li>` (a real bug) · U6 `package.json` Tier 1 dependency ·
  U7/U8 `generateRegistry.mjs` — **U8 is notable: the fix silently no-ops because
  `BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA` was not bumped.**
- **Disputed — reply, do not apply:** U4 breadcrumb leaf category. This is a **CodeRabbit
  loop** — raised 3×, reverted 2× (`47ad72b`, `0ec26f9`) because it produces
  `Home/New/New/Product`. Applying it re-introduces a known regression.
- **Valid gap, wrong fix:** U3 asks to add `react-helmet` as a new direct dependency — the
  same Hard Rule #7 wall as U6.

Per AGENTS.md, **every** finding needs an in-thread reply whether fixed or not — a fix
commit alone does not count, and silence teaches CodeRabbit nothing.

---

## 9. Blockers and doc conflicts

- **SFCC-26** (the blocking attribute story) is "Ready to **deploy** to UAT" — the AC is
  unproven against real data. Three E2E tests are skipped "pending sandbox product
  provisioning".
- **Subtask SFCC-712 Test Case Execution is To Do.**
- **Confluence 04.72** puts PDP stories "ready for development" at **24 Aug** (today is the
  22nd); **04.7** lists Product Content as *"Done, minor update required"* — the design is
  not locked.
- **Scope double-booking:** **SFCC-737 `pdp/product-content`** (epic SFCC-2, Ready For
  Review) claims "product name, description, model description, style code" — verbatim
  SFCC-89. **SFCC-723 `pdp/hero`** arguably owns the layout. Confluence 04.71 says Level 2
  page stories must **not** repeat Level 1 component build detail.
- **Breadcrumb is cross-squad contested:** **SFCC-578 "SEO — Breadcrumb Component (PLP &
  PDP)"** is Squad B, epic SFCC-22, still To Do, describing the same component, with
  SFCC-573/570 depending on it.
- **`.docs/prd/pdp.md` marks PRD-023/PRD-025 confirmed, but Confluence 04.1.8 has both
  struck through / out of scope** — the local mirror is stale.
- **`.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` still says "Sprint 0 in progress"** and dates Sprint 3 as
  27 Jul–7 Aug vs Jira's 10–24 Aug. Do not rely on it. `projectState.md` has no record of
  this work at all.

---

## 10. Honest verdict

**Solid component base, unsafe integration.** `PdpProductInfo` plus its `ZimmPdpProductInfo`
theme recipe is genuinely exemplary for this codebase — correct Zimm-prefixed naming, proper
registration, no bare scale keys, real a11y work rather than claimed a11y work. The
component layer should be carried forward largely verbatim.

It cannot merge until four **decisions** land — dependency approval, PDP-replacement scope,
breadcrumb-shadow strategy, UI Designer sign-off — and two of those may restructure a
meaningful slice of the code. **Do not rebase-and-continue.** Resolve the decisions first,
then carry the component layer forward. Roughly a day of code work once unblocked.

### Decision-independent work (safe to start now)
5 lint errors (auto-fixable) · 4 untranslated strings · missing `data-testid` on the `h1` ·
8 `var(--zimm-*)` sites moving from JSX into the recipe · mobile padding 32→30 · info column
360→218.

### Blocked on decisions
Page composition · sanitiser + SSR crash · `modelFit` vs `c_sizeFit` · breadcrumb ownership ·
anything touching `typography.ts` (Tier 1).

All three confirmed. Two are corrections I need to own:

**My "move all 8 `var(--zimm-*)` sites into the recipe" advice was wrong.** `theme/index.ts` registers `borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space`, `textStyles` — and **not `sizes`**. The three disputed sites are `Skeleton height=`, a *sizing* prop, so a bare token key there would resolve against an unregistered scale and blow up or vanish. `var(--zimm-scale-*)` is the **correct** form in those three, not a violation. input.content:
# Verified corrections — supersede FINDINGS-CONSOLIDATED.md where they conflict

Every item below was verified by direct command output on branch
`feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1` on 2026-08-22, AFTER the
consolidated findings were written. **Where this file and `FINDINGS-CONSOLIDATED.md`
disagree, THIS FILE WINS.**

---

## C1. P0-A was wrong: there is ONE shadowing mechanism, not two — and the fix is 3 lines

`FINDINGS-CONSOLIDATED.md` §2 P0-A claims the base PDP is shadowed by two independent
mechanisms and that deleting the route entry "does not fix it". **That is incorrect.**

`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`, own doc comment:

> *"Helper function that returns true only if the import request points to a package in
> 'extends' and the issuer path (the file making the import request) is not located in the
> overrides dir. If true, we re-route the import request to the overrides dir. **If false,
> the import request proceeds to the base package in node_modules**"*

Base `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:43` is:

```js
const ProductDetail = loadable(() => import('./pages/product-detail'), {fallback})
```

A **relative** specifier. It does not name a package in `extends`, so `isFromExtends` is
false and it resolves to the **base** page, not the override.

**Build evidence:** `build/pages-product-detail.js` contains markers from **both** modules —
`product-details-page` (override) ×1 and `RecommendedProducts`/`addToCart` (base) ×3. Both
pages are in the bundle because both are reachable by different routes.

**Therefore:** the ONLY reason the override page is reachable is the explicit entry at
`overrides/app/routes.tsx:38-40`. **Removing those three lines returns `/product/:productId`
to the full base PDP**, restoring add-to-bag, swatches, quantity picker, recommendations,
accordions, `<Helmet>`, 404 handling and SSR cache headers.

**Consequence for planning:** the capability-loss regression is a 3-line revert, NOT a
restructure. The trade-off is that `PdpProductInfo` then renders nowhere, so delivering
SFCC-89 still requires composing it into the base page — but the *regression* and the
*delivery* are now separable, which they were not under the two-mechanism reading. Severity
unchanged; remediation cost far lower.

---

## C2. Three of the eight `var(--zimm-*)` JSX sites are CORRECT and must not be "fixed"

`FINDINGS-CONSOLIDATED.md` §7 lists 8 `var(--zimm-*)`-in-JSX sites as violations, and §10
lists "8 `var(--zimm-*)` sites moving from JSX into the recipe" as safe decision-independent
work. **Partly wrong — acting on it would introduce a live layout bug.**

`overrides/app/theme/index.ts:52-57` registers exactly:
`borderWidths`, `breakpoints`, `colors`, `fonts`, `space: spacing`, `textStyles`.
**`sizes` is NOT registered.**

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:69-71`:

```tsx
<Skeleton height="var(--zimm-scale-800)" mb="m" />
<Skeleton height="var(--zimm-scale-500)" mb="xl" width="40%" />
<Skeleton height="var(--zimm-scale-5xl)" />
```

`height` is a **sizing** prop, resolving through `theme.sizes` — unregistered. A bare token
key there misresolves or emits nothing. **`var(--zimm-scale-*)` is the correct form in these
three.** Note the author simultaneously used bare keys on `mb` (`m`, `xl`) — a **spacing**
prop, which IS registered. That is correct on both counts.

**Revised tally of the 8 sites:**
- `:69`, `:70`, `:71` — **CORRECT as-is**, leave alone (sizing props)
- `:61`, `:62`(base), `:63` — have named equivalents, safe to move into the recipe
- `:52` (180px) and `:62`(md) (140px) — **genuine token gaps**, no named key exists; needs a
  designer decision, not a mechanical move
- `breadcrumb:33`, `zimmPageToolbar:58` — assess individually by prop type

---

## C3. `auditTokenUsage.mjs` — the broken mandate is the repo's, and it IS citable

The script does not exist (`ls scripts/` — verified). The mandate is **not** in the
local-only build manual; it is in **`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:32`**, a repo file:

> *"Run `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` before opening a PR that touches
> `overrides/app/components/**` or `overrides/app/theme/components/**`"*

Because the broken rule lives in a citable repo file, it can be raised in a PR or issue
directly. Either ship the script or amend the rule.

---

## C4. `.claude/rules/testing.md:87` teaches a broken import

```
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'
```

`node_modules/@storybook/test` **does not exist** on the installed Storybook 10. The
`storybook` package exports `./test` (verified: `exports['./test']` is present). The author
ignored the rule and imported correctly. **A citable repo rules file is actively teaching a
pattern that fails.**

---

## C5. Ownership is a THREE-way disagreement, and PR #57 widened it

| Source | Squad | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| `CODEOWNERS:159` | **Squad B** | — |
| `.claude/rules/squadA.md:4,34` | Squad A | — |
| `.claude/registry/pages.md:20` | Squad A | 4 — Feature-local |

PR #57 moves `'app/pages/product-detail/'` from `SQUAD_B_PATHS` to `SQUAD_A_PATHS` in
`scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`, so the generated registry now actively contradicts the only
surface GitHub enforces.

**This was already decided.** The `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` §16.4 item 1
recorded this exact contradiction on **2026-07-09** — six weeks before it blocked this PR —
and L421 gives the tie-break verbatim: *"whichever `CODEOWNERS` says."* **CODEOWNERS says

1. `VERIFIED-CORRECTIONS.md` — **HIGHEST AUTHORITY.** Every item was verified by direct command output. Where anything else disagrees with this file, this file wins. It contains corrections to the original findings, including one that materially reduces remediation cost.
2. `FINDINGS-CONSOLIDATED.md` — the base investigation. Accurate except where superseded above.
3. The four audits: `audit-uibuild.md`, `audit-fedlead.md`, `audit-fedbuild.md`, `audit-zimmlead.md`
4. Detail sources if you need them: `req-jira.md`, `req-figma.md`, `code-state.md`, `pr57-review.md`, `conventions.md`, `pr57-body.md`

## Subject
PR #57 / SFCC-89 "PDP UI static product information". Author **JhoanDelaCruz** (not the Lead). Branch `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-ui-static-product-information` @ `d526ad1`, base `develop`. OPEN, CHANGES_REQUESTED (bot-only), MERGEABLE, BLOCKED. The Lead is taking it over and has deliberately DEFERRED four decisions: page composition, ticket scope/ownership, sanitiser + Tier 1 dependency, and PR takeover strategy.

## Required tone — "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead"
This is the defining constraint. It means:
- **Explain every mechanism from first principles, in plain language.** Assume the reader has never seen this specific bug. Walk through what actually happens, step by step, in the order it happens. If a webpack resolver rule causes a page to disappear, explain how — do not just assert it.
- **Assume total technical fluency and full decision authority.** They know React, webpack, Chakra, CI, SFCC. Never explain what a prop is. Never say "as you may know". Never condescend.
- **Lead with consequence, then mechanism, then the fix.** "Merging this removes add-to-bag" before "path shadowing".
- Short paragraphs. Concrete nouns. No filler, no throat-clearing, no motivational padding.
- Every claim carries evidence: `file:line`, a command and its output, a ticket key, or a verbatim quote.
- Plain prose over jargon, but never at the cost of precision. Use the real term, then explain it.

## What the report must do

**1. ADJUDICATE CONFLICTS.** The four audits disagree in places, and some contradict the base findings. Find every conflict and rule on it, showing your reasoning and evidence. Known conflicts to resolve (there may be more — look):
   - One audit says the `ui-kits` convention is "unsettled"; another says the build manual covers it thoroughly and explicitly rules in favour of `overrideStyling.md`, rejecting the competing Emotion/`.styles.ts` model. Which is right, and what does the Lead actually tell the team?
   - The number of shadowing mechanisms (see `VERIFIED-CORRECTIONS.md` C1 — this is settled, but make sure the report does not repeat the superseded version anywhere).
   - How many `var(--zimm-*)` JSX sites are genuine violations (see C2 — again settled, but check the audits do not contradict it).
   - Whether `auditTokenUsage.mjs` is mandated by a citable repo file or only a local doc (C3).
   - Any disagreement about what is/is not CI-gated.

**2. RANK EVERYTHING BY WHAT IT COSTS TO IGNORE.** Not by severity label — by consequence. A three-line fix that prevents a storefront regression outranks a fifteen-file refactor that improves consistency.

**3. SEPARATE THE FOUR BUCKETS CLEANLY:**
   - **Do now** — decision-independent, safe, no approvals needed. Give exact file:line and the change.
   - **Blocked on a decision** — say which of the four decisions, and what each option costs.
   - **Blocked on another person** — name the role and the specific ask. (Integration for Hard Rule #7; UI Designer for `typography.ts` and the six off-scale spacing values; Squad B for CODEOWNERS approval and SFCC-578; Jas for ticket scope.)
   - **Not ours / log and move on** — with the owning ticket key.

**4. BE SCRUPULOUSLY FAIR TO THE AUTHOR.** A large share of what went wrong is process failure, not developer failure. `VERIFIED-CORRECTIONS.md` C9 lists these and C10 lists what the branch got genuinely right. The report must make it impossible to read this as a hit piece. State plainly which failures are the *organisation's* — the reviewing side in particular: the preview URL sat unopened for four days, five reviewer teams ignored the request, and three separate repo rules files are broken, missing, or teaching wrong patterns.

**5. FIX THE DOCUMENTATION.** Across the four audits there are many proposed corrections to the reference docs and to the repo's own `.claude/rules/`. Consolidate them into one prioritised list, separating: (a) repo files that are wrong and citable, so fixing them is normal work; (b) local-only docs that need correcting for the Lead's own use.

**6. GIVE A RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE.** End with the order you would actually do this in, with rough effort. Be honest about what is a day and what is an afternoon.

## Hard rules
- **The four reference docs are LOCAL-ONLY.** `uiBuild-knowledge.md`, `fedLead-playbook.md`, `fedBuild-manual.md`, `zimmermann_frontend_lead_playbook.md` must NEVER be cited in a PR, commit message, or code comment. Where a rule also exists in `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/`, cite the repo file as the citable source and say so. Flag anywhere the ONLY source is a local doc — that is a gap needing a repo rule.
- Quote verbatim when you quote. Never paraphrase and present it as a quote.
- Distinguish VERIFIED from inferred, every time.
- Do not invent design values, rules, or ticket numbers.
- If something genuinely cannot be determined, say so rather than filling the gap.

## Output
Write the report to **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/SFCC-89_PR57-takeover-report.md`**

Make it navigable: a title, a dated header line, a short "read this first" summary (10 lines max, the things that change what the Lead does today), then a table of contents, then the body. Use tables where they compress well. Use headings the reader can scan. It should be genuinely useful opened cold in three weeks.

Then give a condensed version in your final report message — leading with the adjudicated conflicts and the "do now" list.

All four audits are in and the collator is writing the report to `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/SFCC-89_PR57-takeover-report.md`, alongside the four docs it audited.

Two things worth knowing before it lands, because they change the shape of the work:

**The regression is a three-line fix.** I told you earlier that deleting the route entry wouldn't help because path-shadowing would replace the PDP anyway. That was wrong. The resolver only redirects imports that *name* a package in `extends`, and base `routes.jsx:43` uses a relative `import('./pages/product-detail')` — so it resolves to the base page untouched. The override is reachable *only* via `overrides/app/routes.tsx:38-40`. Remove those lines and the full base PDP comes back. The build confirms it: both modules are present in `build/pages-product-detail.js`. This separates the regression from the delivery, which the two-mechanism reading did not.

**Don't act on my "move all 8 `var()` sites into the recipe" advice.** Three of them are `Skeleton height=` — a sizing prop — and `theme/index.ts` registers `space` but not `sizes`. A bare token key there misresolves. `var(--zimm-scale-*)` is correct in those three; only three should move, and two more are genuine token gaps with no named key at all.

The audits also turned up defects nobody had flagged: **zero `_focusVisible` anywhere on the branch** (with `_hover` implemented two different ways in two components, neither in the recipe), and a Tier 1 governance file — `frozenFiles.md` — asserting fonts are self-hosted on every tier when **zero font files exist on `develop` or HEAD**. That last one means no type metric on this PR has ever been visually validated, since everything rendered against a ~13%-wider fallback.

On fairness, which I've made a required section rather than a footnote: the preview URL sat unopened for four days, five reviewer teams ignored the request, `eslint`/`prettier`/`tsc` are gated by nothing, "build it in Storybook" is structurally impossible for a page here because the fix lives in a Tier 1 frozen file, and three separate repo rules files are missing, broken, or teaching a wrong import. Yes — **two** dedicated tickets, and neither belongs to SFCC-89.

| | SFCC-749 | SFCC-748 |
|---|---|---|
| Title | Disclaimer – PWA Kit Component | Disclaimer – Contentful Component |
| Scope | The React component | The Contentful content type |
| Status | In Refinement | In Refinement |
| Epic | **SFCC-3 Navigation** | **SFCC-3 Navigation** |
| Owner | Isabel Chaloner (Squad A) | Isabel Chaloner (Squad A) |
| Created | 17 Aug, updated 19 Aug | 17 Aug, updated 19 Aug |

They're linked to each other as *Relates*, and both point at the **design system** file (`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm`, node `2083-54022`) — not the composed-page file we've been working from for SFCC-89.

**What it actually is**, per SFCC-749 verbatim:

> *"The Disclaimer component is separate from the Footer component and renders above it on relevant pages."*

Three elements — a left-aligned title (e.g. `TERMS AND CONDITIONS`), a body paragraph, and a `READ MORE` link. All three Contentful-driven, explicitly not hardcoded. Hover/focus/active states are out of scope for 749, deferred to the UI kit. Content authoring is Zimmermann's; Accenture's scope is the schema plus initial entry setup.

**Nothing is built.** No Disclaimer component in `overrides/`, and no equivalent in base SFCC either. The only repo hits are translation JSON files.

Three things worth your attention:

**SFCC-749 has a broken self-link.** Its description says *"see companion Contentful story SFCC-749"* — pointing at itself. It should point to SFCC-748. Trivial, but it means anyone following the link goes in a circle.

**It's a shell component, not a PDP one.** Sitting under the Navigation epic and rendering above the footer, it lands in the same Tier 2 global-shell territory as `header/` and `footer/`. So it's cleanly outside SFCC-89 — good news for the scope boundary, and one fewer thing to argue about on PR #57.

**SFCC-750 "Footer – PWA Kit Component" was created alongside these two**, also under Navigation, also In Refinement, also Isabel's. You already have the footer built under SFCC-55 in PR #59. That's the same duplicate-scope pattern as SFCC-737 vs SFCC-89 — a second instance of the same decomposition problem, which strengthens the case for raising it as a systemic issue rather than ticket-by-ticket.

One caveat on the design: our Figma extraction found no disclaimer in the PDP node, but `get_metadata` failed on that node's size (67 children, >315 KB against the SSE cap), so we never enumerated the full page. Absence from our extract isn't proof it's absent from the design. If you're seeing a disclaimer band in the PDP mockup, it'd be rendering there as the shell component from SFCC-749, not as PDP content.

Separately — there's a *different* disclaimer in the docs: Confluence's TSD on product attributes notes that `Season` *"is used into the PDP product-badge disclaimer text"* in Magento today. That's PDP-specific badge copy, unrelated to the shell band, and I don't see a ticket for it. Say the word if that's the one you meant.

**Zero traces.** Four searches, all clean:

| Search | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `text ~ "dompurify" OR "purify"` | Jira SFCC (incl. comments) | 0 issues |
| `text ~ "sanitize"/"sanitise"/"sanitization"/"sanitisation"` | Jira SFCC | 0 issues |

| sanitize / XSS / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | Confluence SFCC | only incidental "HTML" matches, nothing on sanitisation |

So there's no approval ticket, no TSD, no spike, no ADR, and no Jira comment anywhere. The only written record of this dependency existing is the PR body — which says the approval is needed and hasn't been obtained — plus CodeRabbit's U6 finding.

**The important part is what the search turned up instead.** This project has a documented, demonstrably-used pattern for exactly this situation, and it was followed twice for other dependencies:

**TSD-SFCC-681 (MRT Application Topology)** states it outright:

> *"Declaring it requires integration-team approval under AGENTS.md Hard Rule #7, which is a prerequisite for this work, not a detail"*
> *"Adding undici as a declared dependency needs integration-team approval under Hard Rule #7. The implementing ticket can stall awaiting these"*

**SFCC-662 "Adyen — Install npm Package, Wire SSR Routes & Build Checkout Pages (PWA)"** goes further — the npm install got its *own dedicated story*, sitting at Ready for Development under the Adyen epic.

And the **Story Workflow** page specifies where approvals are meant to live:

> *"Use comments to make decisions, blockers, handoffs, and approvals visible to the wider team"*

There are no such comments on SFCC-89.

**What this means for your Tier 1 conversation.** The gap isn't a missing process — the process exists, is written down, and was applied to `undici` and to the Adyen SDK inside the same project. That removes "nobody knew" as an explanation and makes this straightforwardly a step that got skipped. It also gives you the template for fixing it: a short TSD or a ticket that names Hard Rule #7, states the requirement, and records Integration's decision.

Worth pairing with the technical finding when you raise it — the ask isn't really "approve this package". It's "this package instantiates JSDOM at import time and is why the PDP 500s on every SSR request, so we want to remove it rather than approve it." That's a much easier conversation, and it closes the P0 and the governance breach in one move.

The same search also confirmed **SFCC-732** (TC-001, Product Name Typography) and **SFCC-733** (TC-002, Price Typography) exist as Tasks, both To Do — the two styling ACs whose `.product-name` / `.product-price` selectors the component doesn't currently expose.
